units.zh: 梁書卷第四十二 列傳第三十六
units.en: Book of Liang, Volume 42, Biography 36
units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 42, Biography 36

units.zh: 臧盾 弟厥 傅岐
units.en: Zang Dun; his younger brother Jue; Fu Qi
units.literal: Zang Dun; younger brother Jue; Fu Qi

units.zh: 臧盾字宣卿，東莞莒人。
units.en: Zang Dun, styled Xuanqing, came from Ju in Dongguan.
units.literal: Zang Dun, courtesy name Xuanqing, was a native of Ju in Dongguan.

units.zh: 高祖燾，宋左光祿大夫。
units.en: His great-grandfather Tao had served Song as Left Glorious Grand Master.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Tao had been Left Glorious Grand Master under Song.

units.zh: 祖潭之，左民尚書。
units.en: His grandfather Tanzhi had been Minister of the Left for the People.
units.literal: His grandfather Tanzhi had been Minister of the Left for the People.

units.zh: 父未甄，博涉文史，有才幹，少爲外兄汝南周顒所知。
units.en: His father Weizhen read widely in letters and history and showed real talent; as a youth he came to the attention of his uncle by marriage, Zhou Yong of Runan.
units.literal: His father Weizhen was broadly learned in letters and history and gifted in affairs; in youth he won the notice of his maternal cousin Zhou Yong of Runan.

units.zh: 宋末，起家爲領軍主簿，所奉卽齊武帝。
units.en: At the end of Song he took his first post as recorder on the staff of the Army of the Capital—the lord he served was Emperor Wu of Qi.
units.literal: At the end of Song he began office as recorder in the headquarters of the Army of the Capital; the lord he served was Emperor Wu of Qi.

units.zh: 入齊，歷太尉祭酒、尚書主客郎、建安、廬陵二王府記室、前軍功曹史、通直郎、南徐州中正、丹陽尹丞。
units.en: Under Qi he served as libationer to the Grand Marshal, gentleman for foreign guests in the Ministry of Rites, secretariat aide to the princes of Jian'an and Luling, merit officer on the Forward Army staff, direct-communication attendant, rectifier of the South Xuzhou central register, and assistant to the governor of Danyang.
units.literal: Entering Qi he held posts as libationer to the Grand Marshal, gentleman in the Ministry of Rites in charge of foreign guests, secretariat aide to the princes of Jian'an and Luling, merit officer in the Forward Army, palace attendant for direct communication, rectifier of the central register of South Xuzhou, and assistant in the yamen of the governor of Danyang.

units.zh: 高祖平京邑，霸府建，引爲驃騎刑獄參軍。
units.en: When the High Ancestor secured the capital and set up his headquarters, Weizhen was brought onto the staff of General of Agile Cavalry as penal and judicial aide.
units.literal: When the High Ancestor pacified the capital region and established the hegemon's headquarters, Weizhen was brought in as penal and judicial aide on the staff of General of Agile Cavalry.

units.zh: 天監初，除後軍諮議中郎、南徐州別駕，入拜黃門郎，遷右軍安成王長史、少府卿。
units.en: At the start of Heavenly Surveillance he became staff adviser and middle director in the Rear Army and chief clerk of South Xuzhou, then entered court as a Yellow Gate gentleman and rose to chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng of the Right Army and minister of the palace supplies.
units.literal: At the opening of Heavenly Surveillance he was made staff adviser and middle director in the Rear Army and chief clerk of South Xuzhou, then entered court as gentleman in the Yellow Gate, and was promoted to chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng of the Right Army and minister of the palace supplies.

units.zh: 出爲新安太守，有能名。
units.en: Sent out as magistrate of Xin'an, he earned a reputation for competence.
units.literal: He went out as magistrate of Xin'an and won a name for ability.

units.zh: 還爲太子中庶子、司農卿、太尉長史。
units.en: Recalled, he became Junior Mentor in the heir apparent's household, Chamberlain for the National Granaries, and chief clerk to the Grand Marshal.
units.literal: Returning he became junior tutor to the crown prince, minister of the national granaries, and chief clerk to the Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 丁所生母憂，三年廬于墓側。
units.en: He mourned his birth mother and for three years lived in a hut by the grave.
units.literal: He entered mourning for his birth mother and for three years dwelt in a hut beside the grave.

units.zh: 服闋，除廷尉卿。
units.en: When mourning ended he was appointed minister of justice.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was made minister of justice.

units.zh: 出爲安成王長史、江夏太守，卒官。
units.en: He left the capital as chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng and magistrate of Jiangxia, and died in office.
units.literal: He went out as chief clerk to the Prince of Ancheng and magistrate of Jiangxia, and died in office.

units.zh: 盾幼從徵士琅邪諸葛璩受《五經》，通章句。
units.en: As a youth Dun studied the Five Classics under the recluse Zhuge Huan of Langye and mastered chapter and phrase.
units.literal: In youth Dun studied the Five Classics from the reclusive scholar Zhuge Huan of Langye, mastering chapter and phrase.

units.zh: 璩學徒常有數十百人，盾處其間，無所狎比。
units.en: Huan's pupils often ran to dozens, but Dun kept company with none of them.
units.literal: Huan's students often numbered in the dozens, yet among them Dun kept close with no one.

units.zh: 璩異之，歎曰：「此生重器，王佐才也。」
units.en: Huan marked him out and sighed, "This boy is a heavy vessel—the makings of a king's counselor."
units.literal: Huan marveled at him and sighed: "This youth is a vessel of weight—the stuff of a king's aide."

units.zh: 初爲撫軍行參軍，遷尚書中兵郎。
units.en: He began as traveling aide on the Forward Army staff and was promoted to gentleman in the Secretariat bureau of soldiers.
units.literal: He first served as traveling aide on the staff of the Forward Army and was promoted to gentleman in the Secretariat bureau of soldiers.

units.zh: 盾美風姿，善舉止，每趨奏，高祖甚悅焉。
units.en: Dun was handsome in bearing and graceful in manner; each time he hurried to audience the Founding Emperor took great delight in him.
units.literal: Dun had a handsome bearing and graceful carriage; whenever he hurried to audience the Founding Emperor was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 入兼中書通事舍人，除安右錄事參軍，舍人如故。
units.en: He entered court as concurrent communications attendant in the Secretariat, was made recording aide on the right of stability, and kept his attendant post.
units.literal: He entered court concurrently as communications attendant in the Secretariat, was made recording aide on the right of stability, and kept his post as attendant.

units.zh: 盾有孝性，隨父宿直於廷尉，母劉氏在宅，夜暴亡，左手中指忽痛，不得寢。
units.en: Dun was deeply filial. He followed his father on night duty at the court of justice while his mother Liu stayed at home. That night she died suddenly; the middle finger of his left hand throbbed with pain and he could not sleep.
units.literal: Dun was deeply filial; he followed his father on night duty at the court of justice, while his mother Liu remained at home. She died suddenly that night; the middle finger of his left hand throbbed with pain and he could not sleep.

units.zh: 及曉，宅信果報凶問，其感通如此。
units.en: At dawn a messenger from home brought word of her death—such was the reach of his feeling.
units.literal: At dawn a messenger from the house brought word of death—his sensitivities worked thus.

units.zh: 服制未終，父又卒，盾居喪五年，不出廬戶，形骸枯顇，家人不復識。
units.en: Before her mourning had ended his father died too; Dun mourned five years without leaving the hut, wasted to bone until his family could no longer know him.
units.literal: Before the mourning period for her had ended his father also died; Dun kept mourning five years without leaving the hut, his frame wasted to bone until kin could no longer recognize him.

units.zh: 鄉人王端以狀聞，高祖嘉之，敕累遣抑譬。
units.en: A townsman, Wang Duan, reported this to the throne; the Founding Emperor praised him and again and again sent orders urging him to moderate his grief.
units.literal: A townsman named Wang Duan reported this to the throne; the Founding Emperor praised him and repeatedly sent orders urging restraint.

units.zh: 服闋，除丹陽尹丞，轉中書郎，復兼中書舍人，遷尚書左丞，爲東中郎武陵王長史，行府州國事，領會稽郡丞。
units.en: When mourning ended he became assistant to the governor of Danyang, then Secretariat gentleman, again concurrent Secretariat attendant, then left assistant in the Secretariat, and chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling of the Eastern Army with charge of prefectural and princely affairs and concurrent assistant magistrate of Kuaiji.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was made assistant in the yamen of the governor of Danyang, then promoted to gentleman of the Secretariat, again concurrently attendant in the Secretariat, promoted to left assistant in the Secretariat, and made chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling of the Eastern Army with charge of the prefecture and state affairs and concurrently assistant magistrate of Kuaiji commandery.

units.zh: 還除少府卿，領步兵校尉，遷御史中丞。
units.en: Recalled, he became minister of the palace supplies and colonel of the infantry guard, then censor-in-chief.
units.literal: Returning he was made minister of the palace supplies and colonel of the infantry guard, then promoted to censor-in-chief.

units.zh: 盾性公強，居憲臺甚稱職。
units.en: Dun was upright and forceful by nature and proved highly capable at the censorate.
units.literal: Dun was by nature upright and forceful; in the censorate he proved highly capable.

units.zh: 中大通五年二月，高祖幸同泰寺開講，設四部大會，衆數萬人。
units.en: In the second month of the fifth year of Zhongdatong, the High Ancestor went to Tongtai Temple to open a lecture and held a great assembly of the four orders, with tens of thousands present.
units.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Zhongdatong the Founding Emperor visited Tongtai Temple to open a lecture and held a great assembly in four sections with tens of thousands present.

units.zh: 南越所獻馴象，忽於衆中狂逸，乘轝羽衛及會皆駭散，惟盾與散騎郎裴之禮嶷然自若，高祖甚嘉焉。
units.en: A tame elephant from Southern Yue suddenly ran wild in the crowd; the imperial carriage guards, feathered guards, and the whole assembly fled in terror. Only Dun and Scattered Cavalry Gentleman Pei Zhili stood unmoved, to the High Ancestor's great admiration.
units.literal: A tame elephant presented by Southern Yue suddenly went mad in the crowd; carriage guards and attendants and the assembly all scattered in terror—only Dun and the regular palace attendant Pei Zhili stood unmoved, to the Founding Emperor's great admiration.

units.zh: 俄有詔，加散騎常侍，未拜，又詔曰：「總一六軍，非才勿授。
units.en: Soon an edict made him regular palace attendant, but before he took office another edict said, "To command the Six Armies—give the post only to the worthy.
units.literal: Soon an edict added him as regular palace attendant, but before he took office another edict said: "To command the Six Armies—give the post only to talent.

units.zh: 御史中丞、新除散騎常侍盾，志懷忠密，識用詳慎，當官平允，處務勤恪，必能緝斯戎政。
units.en: Censor-in-chief and newly appointed regular palace attendant Dun is loyal at heart and careful in judgment; fair in office and diligent in affairs—surely fit to order these military matters.
units.literal: Censor-in-chief and newly appointed regular palace attendant Dun is loyal at heart and careful in judgment; in office he is fair and in affairs diligent—surely able to order these military matters.

units.zh: 可兼領軍，常侍如故。」
units.en: Let him concurrently command the Army of the Capital while keeping his post as regular attendant."
units.literal: He may concurrently command the Army of the Capital while keeping his post as regular attendant."

units.zh: 大同二年，遷中領軍。
units.en: In the second year of Great Unity he was promoted to commandant of the central army.
units.literal: In the second year of Great Unity he was promoted to commandant of the central army.

units.zh: 領軍管天下兵要，監局事多。
units.en: The commandant controlled the empire's military keys and oversaw many bureaus.
units.literal: The commandant's post controlled the empire's military keys and supervised many bureaus.

units.zh: 盾爲人敏贍，有風力，長於撥繁，職事甚理。
units.en: Dun was quick and capable, forceful in character, and excelled at cutting through complexity; the work ran in good order.
units.literal: Dun was quick and capable, had force of character, and excelled at cutting through complexity—the work ran in good order.

units.zh: 天監中，吳平侯蕭景居此職，著聲稱。
units.en: In Heavenly Surveillance the Marquis of Pingwu, Xiao Jing, had held this post to wide renown.
units.literal: In Heavenly Surveillance the Marquis of Pingwu Xiao Jing had held this post with famed reputation.

units.zh: 至是盾復繼之。
units.en: Now Dun followed him in that line.
units.literal: Now Dun followed him in succession.

units.zh: 五年，出爲仁威將軍、吳郡太守，視事未期，以疾陳解。
units.en: In the fifth year he went out as General of Renowned Might and magistrate of Wu; before half his term was done he pleaded illness and resigned.
units.literal: In the fifth year he went out as General of Renowned Might and magistrate of Wu commandery; before his term was half done he pleaded illness and resigned.

units.zh: 拜光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。
units.en: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple ribbon.
units.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple ribbon.

units.zh: 七年，疾愈，復爲領軍將軍。
units.en: In the seventh year, recovered from illness, he again became commandant of the army.
units.literal: In the seventh year, recovered from illness, he again became commandant of the army.

units.zh: 九年，卒，時年六十六。
units.en: In the ninth year he died at sixty-six.
units.literal: In the ninth year he died at age sixty-six.

units.zh: 卽日有詔舉哀。
units.en: That very day an edict ordered mourning rites for him.
units.literal: That very day an edict ordered mourning rites.

units.zh: 贈侍中，領軍如故。
units.en: He was posthumously made palace attendant and kept his commandant's title.
units.literal: He was posthumously made palace attendant and kept his commandant's title.

units.zh: 給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢布各有差。
units.en: Eastern Garden funerary objects were granted, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, and money and cloth each in fixed amounts.
units.literal: Eastern Garden funerary objects were granted, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, money and cloth each in fixed amounts.

units.zh: 諡曰忠。
units.en: His posthumous title was Loyal.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal.

units.zh: 子長博，字孟弘，桂陽內史。
units.en: His son Changbo, styled Menghong, became interior minister of Guiyang.
units.literal: His son Changbo, styled Menghong, became interior minister of Guiyang.

units.zh: 次子仲博，曲阿令。
units.en: His second son Zhongbo became magistrate of Qu'a.
units.literal: His second son Zhongbo became magistrate of Qu'a.

units.zh: 盾弟厥。
units.en: Dun's younger brother was Jue.
units.literal: Dun's younger brother Jue.

units.zh: 厥字獻卿，亦以幹局稱。
units.en: Jue, styled Xianqing, was also known for administrative talent.
units.literal: Jue, courtesy name Xianqing, was also known for administrative talent.

units.zh: 初爲西中郎行參軍、尚書主客郎。
units.en: He began as traveling aide in the Western Central Command and gentleman in the foreign-guests bureau.
units.literal: He first served as traveling aide in the Western Central Command and gentleman in the foreign-guests bureau.

units.zh: 入兼中書通事舍人，累遷正員郎、鴻臚卿，舍人如故。
units.en: He entered court as concurrent communications attendant, rose to full attendant and minister of guests, and kept his attendant post.
units.literal: He entered court concurrently as communications attendant, rose through full attendant to minister of guests, and kept his attendant post.

units.zh: 遷尚書右丞，未拜，出爲晉安太守。
units.en: Promoted to right assistant in the Secretariat, he did not take office but went out as magistrate of Jin'an.
units.literal: He was promoted to right assistant in the Secretariat; before taking office he went out as magistrate of Jin'an.

units.zh: 郡居山海，常結聚逋逃，前二千石雖募討捕，而寇盜不止。
units.en: The commandery lay among mountains and sea where fugitives often gathered; though earlier magistrates had raised troops to hunt them down, banditry never ceased.
units.literal: The commandery lay among mountains and sea and bandits often gathered; though previous magistrates had raised troops to hunt them, robbery never ceased.

units.zh: 厥下車，宣風化，凡諸凶黨，皆涘負而出，居民復業，商旅流通。
units.en: When Jue took office he proclaimed moral guidance; every violent faction came forward bearing guilt, the people returned to their trades, and merchants traveled freely again.
units.literal: When Jue took office he proclaimed moral guidance; all the violent factions came forward bearing their crimes, the people returned to their trades, and merchants traveled freely again.

units.zh: 然爲政嚴酷少恩，吏民小事必加杖罰，百姓謂之「臧虎」。
units.en: Yet his rule was harsh and showed little grace; officials and commoners were flogged for trifles, and the people called him "Tiger Zang."
units.literal: Yet in government he was harsh and showed little grace; for small matters officials and people alike were flogged, and the folk called him "Tiger Zang."

units.zh: 還除驃騎廬陵王諮議參軍，復兼舍人。
units.en: Recalled, he became staff adviser to the Prince of Luling of Rapid Cavalry and again concurrent attendant.
units.literal: Returning he was made staff adviser to the Prince of Luling of Rapid Cavalry and again concurrent attendant.

units.zh: 遷員外散騎常侍，兼司農卿，舍人如故。
units.en: He rose to exterior regular palace attendant and concurrently minister of the national granaries, keeping his attendant post.
units.literal: He was promoted to exterior regular palace attendant and concurrently minister of the national granaries, attendant as before.

units.zh: 大同八年，卒官，時年四十八。
units.en: In the eighth year of Great Unity he died in office at forty-eight.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Great Unity he died in office at age forty-eight.

units.zh: 厥前後居職，所掌之局大事及蘭臺廷尉所不能決者，敕並付厥。
units.en: Throughout his career the major matters of the bureaus he ran—and cases the Orchid Terrace and court of justice could not settle—were all entrusted to Jue.
units.literal: Throughout his career the major matters of the bureaus he ran—and cases the Orchid Terrace and court of justice could not decide—were all entrusted to Jue.

units.zh: 厥辨斷精詳，咸得其理。
units.en: Jue's judgments were precise and detailed, and all accorded with reason.
units.literal: Jue's judgments were precise and detailed; all accorded with reason.

units.zh: 厥卒後，有撾登聞鼓訴者，求付清直舍人。
units.en: After Jue died someone beat the petition drum at the Gate of Impartial Hearing, asking that his cases be given to a fair and upright attendant.
units.literal: After Jue died someone beat the petition drum at the Gate of Impartial Hearing, asking that his cases be given to a fair and upright attendant.

units.zh: 高祖曰：「臧厥旣亡，此事便無可付。」
units.en: The Founding Emperor said, "Now that Zang Jue is gone, there is no one to whom this can be entrusted."
units.literal: The Founding Emperor said: "Now that Zang Jue is gone, there is no one to whom this can be entrusted."

units.zh: 其見知如此。
units.en: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
units.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

units.zh: 子操，尚書三公郎。
units.en: His son Cao was gentleman in the three excellencies bureau of the Secretariat.
units.literal: His son Cao was gentleman in the three excellencies bureau of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 傅岐字景平，北地靈州人也。
units.en: Fu Qi, styled Jingping, came from Lingzhou in Beidi.
units.literal: Fu Qi, courtesy name Jingping, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi.

units.zh: 高祖弘仁，宋太常。
units.en: His great-grandfather Hongren had served Song as grand chamberlain.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Hongren had been grand chamberlain under Song.

units.zh: 祖琰，齊世爲山陰令，有治能，自縣擢爲益州刺史。
units.en: His grandfather Yan, in Qi times magistrate of Shanyin, governed well and was raised from that county post to Inspector of Yi Province.
units.literal: His grandfather Yan, in Qi times magistrate of Shanyin, had governing ability and was promoted from that county post to Inspector of Yi Province.

units.zh: 父翽，天監中，歷山陰、建康令，亦有能名，官至驃騎諮議。
units.en: His father Hui, under Heavenly Surveillance, held Shanyin and Jiankang in succession, likewise famed for ability, and reached staff adviser to Rapid Cavalry.
units.literal: His father Hui, in Heavenly Surveillance, held the magistracies of Shan and Jiankang in succession, likewise famed for ability, and reached staff adviser to Rapid Cavalry.

units.zh: 岐初爲國子明經生，起家南康王宏常侍，遷行參軍，兼尚書金部郎。
units.en: Qi first was a classics fellow in the National University, then began as attendant to Prince Hong of Nankang, rose to traveling aide, and concurrently gentleman in the treasury bureau of gold.
units.literal: Qi first served as a classics fellow in the National University, then began office as attendant to Prince Hong of Nankang, was promoted to traveling aide, and concurrently gentleman in the treasury bureau of gold.

units.zh: 母憂去職，居喪盡禮。
units.en: He left office to mourn his mother and observed every rite to the full.
units.literal: He left office for his mother's mourning and observed the rites to the full.

units.zh: 服闋後，疾廢久之。
units.en: After mourning ended he was long disabled by illness.
units.literal: After mourning ended he was long disabled by illness.

units.zh: 是時改創北郊壇，初起岐監知繕築，事畢，除如新令。
units.en: At that time the northern suburban altar was being rebuilt; Qi was first put in charge of construction, and when the work was finished he was appointed magistrate of Ruxin.
units.literal: At that time the northern suburban altar was being newly built; Qi was first put in charge of supervising construction, and when the work was done he was appointed magistrate of Ruxin.

units.zh: 縣民有因鬬相毆而死者，死家訴郡，郡錄其仇人，考掠備至，終不引咎，郡乃移獄於縣。
units.en: Among the county people two men fought and one died; the dead man's kin sued at the prefecture, which arrested the enemy and tortured him by every means, yet he would not confess; the prefecture then transferred the case to the county.
units.literal: Among the county people two men fought and one died; the dead man's family sued at the prefecture, which arrested the enemy and tortured him through every means, yet he would not confess; the prefecture then transferred the case to the county.

units.zh: 岐卽命脫械，以和言問之，便卽首服。
units.en: Qi at once ordered the shackles removed and questioned him gently; the man confessed on the spot.
units.literal: Qi at once ordered the shackles removed and questioned him in gentle words; the man immediately confessed.

units.zh: 法當償死，會冬節至，岐乃放其還家，使過節一日復獄。
units.en: By law he should pay with his life, but the winter solstice was near; Qi sent him home to pass the festival and return to prison after one day.
units.literal: By law he should pay with his life, but the winter solstice was at hand; Qi then sent him home to pass the festival and return to prison after one day.

units.zh: 曹掾固爭曰：「古者乃有此，於今不可行。」
units.en: The clerks argued firmly, "In antiquity there was such a thing, but in our day it cannot be done."
units.literal: The clerks argued firmly: "In antiquity there was such a thing, but in our day it cannot be done."

units.zh: 岐曰：「其若負信，縣令當坐，主者勿憂。」
units.en: Qi said, "If he breaks faith, the magistrate will bear the penalty—you need not worry."
units.literal: Qi said: "If he breaks faith, the magistrate will bear the penalty—you need not worry."

units.zh: 竟如期而反。
units.en: He returned on the appointed day after all.
units.literal: He returned on the appointed day after all.

units.zh: 太守深相歎異，遽以狀聞。
units.en: The prefect was deeply struck and at once reported it upward.
units.literal: The prefect was deeply struck and at once reported it upward.

units.zh: 岐後去縣，民無老小，皆出境拜送，啼號之聲，聞於數十里。
units.en: Later, when Qi left the county, young and old alike went beyond the border to bow him farewell; the sound of weeping carried for dozens of li.
units.literal: Later, when Qi left the county, young and old alike went beyond the border to bow him farewell; the sound of weeping was heard for dozens of li.

units.zh: 至都，除廷尉正，入兼中書通事舍人，遷寧遠岳陽王記室參軍，舍人如故。
units.en: At the capital he became Rectifier in the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement, entered court as concurrent Palace Secretariat Communications Attendant, was promoted to Record-Office Aide to the Prince of Yueyang, General Who Pacifies Distant, and kept his attendant post.
units.literal: Reaching the capital he was made Rectifier in the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement, entered court concurrently as Palace Secretariat Communications Attendant, was promoted to Record-Office Aide to the Prince of Yueyang, General Who Pacifies Distant, and kept his attendant post as before.

units.zh: 出爲建康令，以公事免。
units.en: He went out as magistrate of Jiankang and was dismissed over an official matter.
units.literal: He went out as magistrate of Jiankang and was dismissed for an official matter.

units.zh: 俄復爲舍人，累遷安西中記室、鎮南諮議參軍，兼舍人如故。
units.en: Soon he was again made attendant and rose through secretariat aide in the Anxi Central Command and staff adviser to the southern pacification army, keeping his attendant post.
units.literal: Soon he was again made attendant and rose through secretariat aide in the Anxi Central Command and staff adviser to the southern pacification army, attendant as before.

units.zh: 岐美容止，博涉能占對。
units.en: Qi had a fine bearing, read widely, and was skilled in repartee.
units.literal: Qi had a fine bearing and was broadly learned, skilled in repartee.

units.zh: 大同中，與魏和親，其使歲中再至，常遣岐接對焉。
units.en: In Great Unity, when Liang and Wei made peace, Wei envoys came twice a year; Qi was often sent to receive them.
units.literal: In Great Unity, when Liang and Wei made peace, their envoys came twice a year; Qi was often sent to receive them.

units.zh: 太清元年，累遷太僕、司農卿，舍人如故。
units.en: In the first year of Supreme Purity he rose in succession to grand charioteer and minister of the national granaries, keeping his attendant post.
units.literal: In the first year of Supreme Purity he rose in succession to grand charioteer and minister of the national granaries, attendant as before.

units.zh: 在禁省十餘年，機事密勿亞於朱异。
units.en: For more than ten years in the forbidden precinct he handled confidential affairs, second only to Zhu Yi.
units.literal: For more than ten years in the forbidden precinct he handled confidential affairs, second only to Zhu Yi.

units.zh: 此年冬，豫州刺史貞陽侯蕭淵明率衆伐彭城，兵敗陷魏。
units.en: That winter Marquis Zhenyang, Xiao Yuanming, governor of Yuzhou, led troops against Pengcheng; the army was defeated and Yuanming fell into Wei hands.
units.literal: That winter Marquis Zhenyang of Xiao Yuanming, governor of Yuzhou, led troops to attack Pengcheng; the army was defeated and Yuanming was taken by Wei.

units.zh: 二年，淵明遣使還，述魏人欲更通和好，敕有司及近臣定議。
units.en: In the second year Yuanming sent envoys back, saying the Wei wished renewed peace; an edict ordered the relevant offices and nearby ministers to decide.
units.literal: In the second year Yuanming sent envoys back, reporting that the Wei wished renewed peace and harmony; an edict ordered the relevant offices and nearby ministers to decide.

units.zh: 左衛朱异曰：「高澄此意，當復欲繼好，不爽前和；
units.en: Left Guard Zhu Yi said, "Gao Cheng's intent is surely to renew good relations and not break the prior peace;
units.literal: Left Guard Zhu Yi said: "Gao Cheng's intent is surely to renew the good relations and not break the prior peace;

units.zh: 邊境且得靜寇息民，於事爲便。」
units.en: the borders may rest from raiders and the people from harm—for affairs this is convenient."
units.literal: the borders may rest from raiders and the people from harm—for affairs this is convenient."

units.zh: 議者並然之。
units.en: The debaters all agreed with him.
units.literal: The debaters all agreed with him.

units.zh: 岐獨曰：「高澄旣新得志，其勢非弱，何事須和？
units.en: Qi alone said, "Gao Cheng has newly secured his aims; his power is not weak—why should he need peace?
units.literal: Qi alone said: "Gao Cheng has newly secured his aims; his power is not weak—why should he need peace?

units.zh: 此必是設間，故令貞陽遣使，令侯景自疑當以貞陽易景。
units.en: This must be a stratagem: he has Zhenyang send envoys so Hou Jing will suspect he is to be exchanged for Zhenyang.
units.literal: This must be a stratagem: he has Zhenyang send envoys so that Hou Jing will suspect he is to be exchanged for Zhenyang.

units.zh: 景意不安，必圖禍亂。
units.en: Uneasy in mind, Jing is sure to plot rebellion.
units.literal: Uneasy in mind, Jing is sure to plot rebellion.

units.zh: 今若許澄通好，正是墮其計中。
units.en: If we now grant Cheng peace, we fall straight into his scheme.
units.literal: If we now grant Cheng peace, we fall straight into his scheme.

units.zh: 且彭城去歲喪師，渦陽新復敗退，令便就和，益示國家之弱。
units.en: Moreover, last year Pengcheng lost its army and Guoyang has newly suffered defeat and retreat—to make peace now only shows the state's weakness.
units.literal: Moreover, last year Pengcheng lost its army and Guoyang has newly suffered defeat and retreat—to make peace now only shows the state's weakness.

units.zh: 若如愚意，此和宜不可許。」
units.en: In my humble view this peace ought not be granted."
units.literal: In my humble view this peace ought not be granted."

units.zh: 朱异等固執，高祖遂從異議。
units.en: Zhu Yi and the rest held firm; the Founding Emperor followed Yi's counsel.
units.literal: Zhu Yi and the rest held firm; the Founding Emperor followed Yi's counsel.

units.zh: 及遣和使，侯景果有此疑，累啟請追使，敕但依違報之。
units.en: When peace envoys were sent, Hou Jing indeed harbored this suspicion and repeatedly memorialized asking that the envoys be recalled; edicts answered only evasively.
units.literal: When peace envoys were sent, Hou Jing indeed harbored this suspicion and repeatedly memorialized asking that the envoys be recalled; edicts answered only evasively.

units.zh: 至八月，遂舉兵反。
units.en: By the eighth month he had raised troops in rebellion.
units.literal: By the eighth month he had raised troops in rebellion.

units.zh: 十月，入寇京師，請誅朱异。
units.en: In the tenth month he invaded the capital and asked that Zhu Yi be executed.
units.literal: In the tenth month he invaded the capital and asked that Zhu Yi be executed.

units.zh: 三年，遷中領軍，舍人如故。
units.en: In the third year he was promoted to commandant of the central army, keeping his attendant post.
units.literal: In the third year he was promoted to commandant of the central army, attendant as before.

units.zh: 二月，景于闕前通表，乞割江右四州，安其部下，當解圍還鎮，敕許之。
units.en: In the second month Jing submitted a memorial before the palace gate, asking to cede the four prefectures west of the river to settle his followers and promising to lift the siege and return to garrison if granted; an edict approved.
units.literal: In the second month Jing submitted a memorial before the palace gate, asking to cede the four prefectures west of the river to settle his followers and promising to lift the siege and return to garrison if granted; an edict approved.

units.zh: 乃於城西立盟，求遣宣城王出送。
units.en: An oath was then sworn west of the city, and Jing asked that the Prince of Xuancheng be sent out as hostage.
units.literal: An oath was then sworn west of the city, and Jing asked that the Prince of Xuancheng be sent out as hostage.

units.zh: 岐固執宣城嫡嗣之重，不宜許，遣石城公大款送之。
units.en: Qi held firm to the weight of Xuancheng's legitimate heir and said he ought not be granted; the Duke of Stone City, Dakuan, was sent instead.
units.literal: Qi held firm to the weight of the legitimate heir of Xuancheng and said he ought not be granted; the Duke of Stone City, Dakuan, was sent instead.

units.zh: 及與景盟訖，城中文武喜躍，望得解圍。
units.en: When the oath with Jing was finished, civil and military men in the city rejoiced, hoping the siege would be lifted.
units.literal: When the oath with Jing was finished, civil and military men in the city rejoiced, hoping the siege would be lifted.

units.zh: 岐獨言於衆曰：「賊舉兵爲逆，未遂求和，夷情獸心，必不可信，此和終爲賊所詐也。」
units.en: Qi alone said to the assembly, "The bandit raised troops in rebellion and has not yet obtained peace; barbarian hearts and beast natures cannot be trusted—this peace will in the end be the bandit's deceit."
units.literal: Qi alone said to the assembly: "The bandit raised troops in rebellion and has not yet obtained peace; barbarian hearts and beast natures cannot be trusted—this peace will in the end be the bandit's deceit."

units.zh: 衆並怨怪之。
units.en: The crowd all resented and blamed him.
units.literal: The crowd all resented and blamed him.

units.zh: 及景背盟，莫不嘆服。
units.en: When Jing broke the oath, none failed to admire Qi.
units.literal: When Jing broke the oath, none failed to admire him.

units.zh: 尋有詔，以岐勤勞，封南豊縣侯，邑五百戶，固辭不受。
units.en: Soon an edict, for Qi's diligence, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Nanfeng with a fief of five hundred households; he firmly refused and did not accept.
units.literal: Soon an edict, for Qi's diligence, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Nanfeng with a fief of five hundred households; he firmly refused and did not accept.

units.zh: 宮城失守，岐帶疾出圍，卒於宅。
units.en: When the palace city fell, Qi, though ill, broke out of the encirclement and died at his house.
units.literal: When the palace city fell, Qi, though ill, broke out of the encirclement and died at his house.

units.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：夫舉事者定於謀，故萬舉無遺策，信哉是言也。
units.en: Yao Cha of Chen, Minister of Personnel, writes: To raise an affair is to fix it in counsel—thus ten thousand undertakings without a missed plan; how true is that saying.
units.literal: Yao Cha of Chen, Minister of Personnel, says: To raise an affair is to fix it in counsel—thus ten thousand undertakings without a missed plan; how true is that saying.

units.zh: 傅岐識齊氏之偽和，可謂善於謀事。
units.en: Fu Qi's discernment of the false peace offered by Qi may be called true skill in planning affairs.
units.literal: Fu Qi's discernment of the falseness of the Qi peace offer may be called skill in planning affairs.

units.zh: 是時若納岐之議，太清禍亂，固其不作。
units.en: Had the court then accepted Qi's counsel, the Supreme Purity calamity would surely not have come to be.
units.literal: Had the court then accepted Qi's counsel, the Supreme Purity calamity would surely not have come to be.

units.zh: 申子曰：「一言倚，天下靡。」
units.en: Master Shen said, "One leaning word, and the realm is swept along."
units.literal: Master Shen said: "One leaning word, and the realm is swept along."

units.zh: 此之謂乎？
units.en: Is this not the sense of it?
units.literal: Is this not the sense of it?

units.zh: 沖母，梁武帝妹新安穆公主，卒於齊世，武帝以沖偏孤，深所鍾愛。
units.en: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, seeing that Chong had been left partially orphaned, doted on him.
units.literal: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, sister of Emperor Wu of Liang; she died in Qi times, and the Emperor, because Chong was a lone orphan, cherished him deeply.

units.zh: 按梁武帝即位後，追尊其父為文皇帝。
units.en: After Liang Wudi's accession he honored his father posthumously as Emperor Wen.
units.literal: According to the note, after Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wen.

units.zh: 王沖傳言其母為梁武帝妹新安穆公主，與此合。
units.en: Wang Chong's biography says his mother was Liang Wudi's sister Princess Xin'an Mu, which matches.
units.literal: The biography of Wang Chong says his mother was Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess Xin'an Mu—this agrees.

units.zh: 王沖 王通弟勱 袁敬兄子樞
units.en: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu
units.literal: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu

units.zh: [2]琳，齊代娶梁武帝妹義興長公主，有子九人，嵭知名。
units.en: Lin, in Qi times, married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess of Yixing long; he had nine sons, all of whom won notice.
units.literal: Lin, in Qi times married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister Princess of Yixing long, had nine sons, and all became renowned.

units.zh: 大同末，梁武帝謁園陵，道出朱方，勱隨例迎候，队勱令從輦側，所經山川，莫不顧問，勱隨事應對，咸有故實。
units.en: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs by way of Zhufang; Mo met him as custom required. The emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; at every hill and stream he asked questions, and Mo answered each with historical precedent.
units.literal: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs; the route passed through Zhufang; Mo greeted him per custom; the Emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; every mountain and river passed, the Emperor inquired; Mo answered each matter with historical precedent.

units.zh: 學申、商刑名於軹張恢生所，與雒陽宋孟及劉帶同師。
units.en: He studied the legalist doctrines of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang under Zhang Huisheng of Zhi, alongside Song Meng of Luoyang and Liu Dai.
units.literal: He studied Shen and Shang penal law and forms at the place of Zhang Huisheng of Zhi, and with Song Meng of Luoyang and Liu Dai he shared the same teacher.

units.zh: 溉，〔一〕時梁州刺史陰子春、領軍朱异在焉。
units.en: Collation variant: (Gai), [1] At that time Liang inspector of Liangzhou Yin Zichun and director of the palace guard Zhu Yi were present.
units.literal: Collation variant: (Gai), At that time Liang Inspector of Liangzhou Yin Zichun and Director of the Palace Guard Zhu Yi were present.

units.zh: 子春素知申，即於坐所呼與為對，〔二〕申每有妙思，异觀而奇之，因引申遊處。
units.en: Zichun had long known Shen and immediately at the gathering called him to play a match, [2] Shen had fine conceptions each time; Yi watched and marveled, and thereafter drew Shen into his company.
units.literal: Zichun had long known Shen and immediately at the gathering called him to play a match, Shen had fine conceptions each time; Yi watched and marveled, and thereafter drew Shen into his company.

units.zh: 時武陵王在東州，頗自驕縱，上召革面敕曰：「武陵王年少，臧盾性弱，不能匡正，欲以卿代爲行事。
units.en: Prince Wuling held East Yangzhou and had grown proud and loose. The emperor summoned Ge and charged him in person: "Prince Wuling is young. Zang Dun is mild and cannot correct him. I want you to replace him as acting administrator.
units.literal: Prince Wuling was in East Yangzhou and rather arrogant and unrestrained; the Emperor summoned Ge and personally charged him: "Prince Wuling is young; Zang Dun is timid by nature and cannot correct him—I wish to have you replace him as acting administrator.

units.zh: 世宗文襄皇帝，諱澄，字子惠，神武長子也，母曰婁太后。
units.en: Emperor Wenxiang, temple name Shizong of Northern Qi, bore the personal name Cheng and the style Zihui. He was the eldest son of Gao Huan; his mother was Empress Dowager Lou.
units.literal: Emperor Shizong Wenxiang, taboo name Cheng, style Zihui, was the eldest son of Shenwu; his mother was Empress Dowager Lou.

units.zh: 王嘗侍飲，舉大觴曰：「臣澄勸陛下酒。」
units.en: Once, while attending him at drink, Gao Cheng raised a great goblet and said, "Your servant Cheng urges Your Majesty to drink."
units.literal: Once, while attending him at drink, the Prince raised a great goblet and said: "Your servant Cheng urges Your Majesty to drink."

units.zh: 齊受禪，追諡為文襄皇帝，廟號世宗。
units.en: When Qi received the abdication, he was posthumously titled Emperor Wenxiang, with the temple name Shizong.
units.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was posthumously titled Emperor Wenxiang, temple name Shizong.

units.zh: 七月戊戌，魏帝詔以文襄為使持節、大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事、大行臺、渤海王。
units.en: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the Eastern Wei emperor issued an edict that Gao Cheng be Bearer of Credentials, Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Prince of Bohai.
units.literal: In the seventh month, on wuxu, the Wei Emperor issued an edict that Wenxiang be Bearer of Credentials, Grand Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief of All Armies at Home and Abroad, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Prince of Bohai.

units.zh: 魏中興元年，立為渤海王世子。
units.en: In Zhongxing 1 (531) he was made heir to the Prince of Bohai.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing of Wei he was established as heir of the Prince of Bohai.

units.zh: 三年，入輔朝政，加領左右、京畿大都督。
units.en: In the third year he entered the capital to assist in governance and was given charge of the Left and Right and made Grand Commander of the Capital Region.
units.literal: In the third year he entered to assist court governance and was given charge of the Left and Right and Grand Commander of the Capital Region.

units.zh: 興和二年，加大將軍，領中書監，仍攝吏部尚書。
units.en: In Xinghe 2 (540) he was made Grand General and Director of the Secretariat Supervisor while still serving as acting Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: In the second year of Xinghe he was given Grand General, Director of the Secretariat Supervisor, and still acted as Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 魏帝詔曰：「旣朝野攸憑，安危所系，不得令遂本懷，須有權奪，可復前大將軍，餘如故。」
units.en: The emperor issued an edict, "Since court and countryside rely on you and safety hangs upon you, I cannot let you follow your wish; authority must be taken by necessity. You may resume your former rank of Grand General; the rest remains as before."
units.literal: The Wei Emperor issued an edict: "Since court and countryside rely on you and safety hangs upon you, I cannot let you follow your original wish; there must be a taking of authority by necessity. You may resume your former rank of Grand General; the rest remains as before."

units.zh: 元象元年，攝吏部尚書。
units.en: In Yuanxiang 1 (538) he served as acting Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang he acted as Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 選人常以年勞為制，文襄乃釐改前式，銓擢唯在得人。
units.en: appointments had been governed by seniority; Gao Cheng reformed the old practice so that selection rested only on finding the right men.
units.literal: appointments had been governed by years of service; Wenxiang then reformed the former practice, and selection and promotion rested only on getting the right men.

units.zh: 二年，加侍中、開府儀同三司，尚孝靜帝妹馮翊長公主，時年十二，神情儁爽，便若成人。
units.en: In the second year he was made Palace Attendant and Grand Lord Equal to Three Imperator and married Princess Chang of Fengyi, Emperor Xiaojing's sister. He was twelve, handsome and spirited, already bearing himself like a man.
units.literal: In the second year he was given Palace Attendant, Grand Lord Equal to Three Imperator, and married the Princess Chang of Fengyi, sister of Emperor Xiaojing; he was then twelve, with a handsome and spirited bearing, already like a grown man.

units.zh: 壬寅，魏帝詔太原公洋攝理軍國，遣中使敦喻。
units.en: On renyin day the emperor issued an edict that Duke of Taiyuan Gao Yang administer military and state affairs and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.
units.literal: On renyin the Wei Emperor issued an edict that Duke of Taiyuan Yang administer military and state affairs, and sent a palace envoy to urge him earnestly.

units.zh: 時王居北城東柏堂蒞政，以寵琅邪公主，欲其來往無所避忌，所有侍衛，皆出於外。
units.en: At the time Gao Cheng held court at the East Cypress Hall in the North City; favoring the Princess of Langye, he wished her comings and goings to be without restraint, and had all guards posted outside.
units.literal: At the time the Prince held court at the East Cypress Hall in the North City; favoring the Princess of Langye, he wished her comings and goings to be without restraint, and had all guards posted outside.

units.zh: 就杜詢講學，敏悟過人，詢甚嘆服。
units.en: He studied under Du Xun; his quickness of mind surpassed all others, and Du Xun came to admire him deeply.
units.literal: He went to Du Xun to study; his quick comprehension surpassed others, and Xun greatly admired him.

units.zh: 天平元年，加使持節、尚書令、大行臺、幷州刺史。
units.en: In Tianping 1 (534) he received Bearer of Credentials, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and the inspectorship of Bing Province.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianping he was given Bearer of Credentials, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Inspector of Bing Province.

units.zh: 辛卯，王遇盜而殂，時年二十九。
units.en: On xinmao Gao Cheng fell to assassins and died; he was twenty-nine.
units.literal: On xinmao the Prince fell to assassins and died; he was twenty-nine.

units.zh: 賊黨去床，因而見殺。
units.en: The assassins dragged him from the bed and killed him.
units.literal: The assassins dragged him from the bed and so he was killed.

units.zh: 葬于峻成陵。
units.en: He was buried at Juncheng Tomb.
units.literal: He was buried at Juncheng Tomb.

units.zh: 王以為信然，謂可誘而致，乃遺景書曰：
units.en: Gao Cheng believed it and thought he could be lured back; he sent Hou Jing a letter saying,
units.literal: The Prince believed it true and thought he could be lured back; he sent Jing a letter saying:

units.zh: 先王與司徒契闊夷險，孤子相依，偏所眷屬，義貫終始，情存歲寒。
units.en: The late king and the Minister of Works shared hardship through peril and isolation; I, his orphan, depended on you—you were his special charge. Righteousness ran from first to last; affection endured through the cold years.
units.literal: The late king and the Minister of Works shared hardship through peril and isolation; I, his orphan, depended on you — you were his special charge. Righteousness ran from first to last; affection endured through the cold years.

units.zh: 待為國士者乃立漆身之節，饋以一餐者便致扶輪之效，況其重於此乎？
units.en: Those treated as men of the state would lay down their lives; one who was fed a single meal would repay with the deed of bracing the wheel—how much more when the bond was weightier than this?
units.literal: Those treated as men of the state would lay down their lives; one who was fed a single meal would repay with the deed of bracing the wheel — how much more when the bond was weightier than this?

units.zh: 常以故舊之義，欲將子孫相托，方為秦晉之匹，共成劉、范之親。
units.en: By the old friendship I ever meant to entrust my descendants to you and make a match like Qin and Jin, forming a kinship like Liu and Fan.
units.literal: By the old friendship I ever meant to entrust my descendants to you and make a match like Qin and Jin, forming a kinship like Liu and Fan.

units.zh: 況聞負杖行歌，便以狼顧反噬，不蹈忠臣之路，便陷叛人之地。
units.en: Yet I hear that leaning on your staff and singing in the lanes, you turned like a wolf to bite in return, forsook the path of the loyal minister, and fell into the land of the rebel.
units.literal: Yet I hear that leaning on your staff and singing in the lanes, you turned like a wolf to bite in return, forsook the path of the loyal minister, and fell into the land of the rebel.

units.zh: 力不足以自強，勢不足以自保，率烏合之衆，為累卵之危。
units.en: Your strength is not enough to strengthen yourself; your power is not enough to protect yourself; you lead a rabble host and stand in peril like a pile of eggs.
units.literal: Your strength is not enough to strengthen yourself; your power is not enough to protect yourself; you lead a rabble host and stand in peril like a pile of eggs.

units.zh: 西取救於宇文，南請援於蕭氏，以狐疑之心，為首鼠之事。
units.en: West you seek rescue from Yuwen; south you ask aid from the Xiao house—with a doubting heart you do the deed of a wavering rat.
units.literal: West you seek rescue from Yuwen; south you ask aid from the Xiao house — with a doubting heart you do the deed of a wavering rat.

units.zh: 入秦則秦人不容，歸吳則吳人不信。
units.en: Enter Qin and the men of Qin will not receive you; return to Wu and the men of Wu will not trust you.
units.literal: Enter Qin and the men of Qin will not receive you; return to Wu and the men of Wu will not trust you.

units.zh: 當是不逞之人，曲為無端之說，遂懷市虎之疑，乃致投杼之惑。
units.en: Surely it was men of disorder who twisted groundless words, so that you harbored the suspicion of the tiger in the market and fell into the confusion of the thrown shuttle.
units.literal: Surely it was men of disorder who twisted groundless words, so that you harbored the suspicion of the tiger in the market and fell into the confusion of the thrown shuttle.

units.zh: 比來舉止，事已可見，人相疑誤，想自覺知。
units.en: Your conduct of late is already plain to see; men suspect and err, and I think you know it yourself.
units.literal: Your conduct of late is already plain to see; men suspect and err, and I think you know it yourself.

units.zh: 闔門大小，悉在司寇，意謂李氏未滅，猶言少卿可反。
units.en: Your whole household, great and small, is in the hands of the Minister of Justice; I thought that since the Li clan was not yet destroyed, one might still say the Lesser Minister could return.
units.literal: Your whole household, great and small, is in the hands of the Minister of Justice; I thought that since the Li clan was not yet destroyed, one might still say the Lesser Minister could return.

units.zh: 孤子無狀招禍，丁天酷罰，但禮由權奪，志在忘私，聊遣偏裨，前驅致討，南兗、揚州，應時剋復。
units.en: I, the orphan, unworthy, have drawn calamity; heaven has dealt a cruel punishment—yet ritual allows taking authority by necessity, and my aim is to forget private feeling. I have sent only a partial force as vanguard to attack; southern Yanzhou and Yangzhou were recovered at once.
units.literal: I, the orphan, unworthy, have drawn calamity; heaven has dealt a cruel punishment — yet ritual allows taking authority by necessity, and my aim is to forget private feeling. I have sent only a partial force as vanguard to attack; southern Yanzhou and Yangzhou were recovered at once.

units.zh: 即欲乘機，席捲縣瓠，屬以炎暑，欲為後圖，且令還師，待時更舉。
units.en: I meant to seize the moment and sweep up Xiangcheng, but because of the heat I planned for later and for now ordered withdrawal, to strike again when the time comes.
units.literal: I meant to seize the moment, sweep up Xiangcheng, but because of the heat I planned for later and for now ordered withdrawal, to strike again when the time comes.

units.zh: 今寒膠向折，白露將團，方憑國靈，龔行天罰。
units.en: Now the cold glue is about to break and white dew will soon gather; relying on the state's numen, I march to execute heaven's punishment.
units.literal: Now the cold glue is about to break and white dew will soon gather; relying on the state's numen, I march to execute heaven's punishment.

units.zh: 器械精新，士馬強盛，內外感恩，上下戮力，三令五申，可赴湯火。
units.en: Weapons are sharp and new, soldiers and horses strong; within and without men are grateful, above and below strive together; thrice and five times commanded, they would walk into boiling water.
units.literal: Weapons are sharp and new, soldiers and horses strong; within and without men are grateful, above and below strive together; thrice and five times commanded, they would walk into boiling water.

units.zh: 使旗鼓相望，埃塵相接，勢如沃雪，事等注熒。
units.en: Banners and drums face each other, dust and smoke meet; the force is like pouring water on snow, the affair like pouring oil on flame.
units.literal: Banners and drums face each other, dust and smoke meet; the force is like pouring water on snow, the affair like pouring oil on flame.

units.zh: 夫明者去危就安，智者轉禍為福，甯人負我，不我負人，當開從善之途，使有改迷之路。
units.en: The clear-sighted leave peril for safety; the wise turn calamity into blessing. Better that others wrong me than that I wrong others—open the path of accepting good, and give a road for correcting error.
units.literal: The clear-sighted leave peril for safety; the wise turn calamity into blessing. Better that others wrong me than that I wrong others — open the path of accepting good, and give a road for correcting error.

units.zh: 若能卷甲來朝，垂橐還闕者，即當授豫州，必使終君身世。
units.en: If you can roll up your armor and come to court, empty your bags and return to the capital, I will at once grant you Yuzhou and see that you hold it for life.
units.literal: If you can roll up your armor and come to court, empty your bags and return to the capital, I will at once grant you Yuzhou and see that you hold it for life.

units.zh: 所部文武更不追攝，進得保其祿位，退則不喪功名。
units.en: Your civil and military subordinates will not be pursued; advance and you keep rank and salary, retreat and you lose neither merit nor fame.
units.literal: Your civil and military subordinates will not be pursued; advance and you keep rank and salary, retreat and you lose neither merit nor fame.

units.zh: 今王思政等皆孤軍偏將，遠來深入，然其性命在君掌握，脫能刺之，想有餘力。
units.en: Now Wang Sizheng and the rest are isolated generals who came from afar and marched deep; yet their lives are in your hand—if you can stab them, I think you still have strength enough.
units.literal: Now Wang Sizheng and the rest are isolated generals who came from afar and marched deep; yet their lives are in your hand — if you can stab them, I think you still have strength enough.

units.zh: 節相加授，永保疆埸。
units.en: I will add the seal of minister and forever secure the frontier.
units.literal: I will add the seal of minister and forever secure the frontier.

units.zh: 君門眷屬，可以無患，寵妻愛子，亦送相還，仍為通家，共成親好。
units.en: Your household kin need not fear; your cherished wife and beloved sons I will also send back—we shall again be allied houses and form a close bond.
units.literal: Your household kin need not fear; your cherished wife and beloved sons I will also send back — we shall again be allied houses and form a close bond.

units.zh: 君今不能東封函谷，南面稱孤，受制於人，威名頓盡。
units.en: If you cannot now seal Hangu Pass in the east and call yourself king facing south, but must be controlled by others, your renown will at once be spent.
units.literal: If you cannot now seal Hangu Pass in the east and call yourself king facing south, but must be controlled by others, your renown will at once be spent.

units.zh: 得地不欲自守，聚衆不以為強，空使身有背叛之名，家有惡逆之禍，覆宗絕嗣，自貽伊戚。
units.en: You gain land yet will not hold it yourself; you gather a host yet do not count it strong—in vain you bear the name of rebel and your house the calamity of treason; clan extinguished, line cut off, you bring sorrow on yourself.
units.literal: You gain land yet will not hold it yourself; you gather a host yet do not count it strong — in vain you bear the name of rebel and your house the calamity of treason; clan extinguished, line cut off, you bring sorrow on yourself.

units.zh: 戴天履地，能無愧乎！
units.en: Wearing heaven on your head and treading earth underfoot—can you be without shame!
units.literal: Wearing heaven on your head and treading earth underfoot — can you be without shame!

units.zh: 孤子今日不應遣此，但見蔡遵道云：「司徒本無西歸之心，深有悔過之意」，未知此語為虛為實。
units.en: I, the orphan, ought not to send this today, but I saw Cai Zundao say, "The Minister of Works originally had no mind to go west and deeply wished to repent"—I do not know whether these words are empty or real.
units.literal: I, the orphan, ought not to send this today, but I saw Cai Zundao say: "The Minister of Works originally had no mind to go west and deeply wished to repent" — I do not know whether these words are empty or real.

units.zh: 吉凶之理，想自圖之。
units.en: The logic of fortune and calamity—I think you will weigh it yourself.
units.literal: The logic of fortune and calamity — I think you will weigh it yourself.

units.zh: 論曰：文襄嗣膺霸道，威略昭著。
units.en: The appraisal says: Wenxiang inherited the hegemonic enterprise, and his power and strategy were unmistakable.
units.literal: The appraisal says: Wenxiang succeeded to the hegemonic enterprise, and his martial strategy was plainly displayed.

units.zh: 而志在峻法，急於禦下，於前王之德，有所未同。
units.en: Yet he set his mind on harsh law and was impatient in ruling those below him; in this he fell short of the former king's virtue.
units.literal: Yet his intent lay in severe laws and he was harsh in governing subordinates; in the virtue of the former king, there was something with which he did not accord.

units.zh: 生而岐嶷，神武異之。
units.en: From birth he was precocious and keen; Gao Huan took him for a prodigy.
units.literal: From birth he was precocious and sharp; Shenwu regarded him as extraordinary.

units.zh: 武定四年十一月，神武西討，不豫班師，文襄馳赴軍所，侍衛還晉陽。
units.en: In the eleventh month of Wuding 4 (546), Gao Huan marched west, fell ill, and withdrew; Gao Cheng raced to the army, attended him, and escorted him back to Jinyang.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Wuding, Shenwu campaigned west and, falling ill, withdrew the army; Wenxiang raced to the army's camp, attended him, and escorted him back to Jinyang.

units.zh: 五年正月丙午，神武崩，秘不發喪。
units.en: In the first month of Wuding 5 (547), on bingwu day, Gao Huan died; the death was kept secret.
units.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, on bingwu, Shenwu died; the death was kept secret.

units.zh: 夏四月壬申，文襄朝於鄴。
units.en: In the fourth month, on renshen day, Gao Cheng attended court at Ye.
units.literal: In the fourth month, on renshen, Wenxiang attended court at Ye.

units.zh: 秘不發喪，徐出言曰：「奴反，大將軍被傷，無大苦也。」
units.en: They kept the death secret, then slowly announced, "The slave rebelled; the Grand General was wounded—nothing grave."
units.literal: They kept the death secret, then slowly announced: "The slave rebelled; the Grand General was wounded—nothing grave."

units.zh: 文襄乃奏吏部郎崔暹為御史中尉，糾劾權豪，無所縱捨，於是風俗更始，私枉路絕。
units.en: Gao Cheng then had Cui Xian of the Ministry of Personnel appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful without sparing any, custom was renewed, and private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.
units.literal: Wenxiang then memorialized to make Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful and wealthy without sparing any, and custom was renewed — private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.

units.zh: 遣司空韓軌率衆討之。
units.en: Gao Cheng sent Minister of Works Han Gui at the head of an army to attack him.
units.literal: He sent Minister of Works Han Gui at the head of an army to attack him.

units.zh: 丁丑，文襄還晉陽，乃發喪，告喻文武，陳神武遺志。
units.en: On dingchou day Gao Cheng returned to Jinyang, announced the death, informed civil and military officials, and set forth Gao Huan's final wishes.
units.literal: On dingchou Wenxiang returned to Jinyang, then announced the death, informed civil and military officials, and set forth Shenwu's final wishes.

units.zh: 文襄啟辭位，願停王爵。
units.en: Gao Cheng memorialized to decline and wished to relinquish the princely rank.
units.literal: Wenxiang memorialized to decline the post and wished to relinquish the princely rank.

units.zh: 八月戊辰，文襄啟申神武遺令，請減國邑分封將督，各有差。
units.en: In the eighth month, on wuchen day, Gao Cheng memorialized to carry out Gao Huan's final command, asking to reduce the royal fief and enfeoff generals and commanders, each according to rank.
units.literal: In the eighth month, on wuchen, Wenxiang memorialized to carry out Shenwu's final command, asking to reduce the fiefs of the realm and enfeoff generals and commanders, each according to rank.

units.zh: 王尋覽書，問誰為作。
units.en: When Gao Cheng had read the letter, he asked who had written it.
units.literal: When the Prince had read the letter, he asked who had written it.

units.zh: 王曰：「偉才如此，何因不使我知？」
units.en: Gao Cheng said, "With talent like this, why was I not told?"
units.literal: The Prince said: "With talent like this, why was I not told?"

units.zh: 王欲間景於梁，又與景書而謬其辭，云本使景陽叛，欲與圖西，西人知之，故景更與圖南為事。
units.en: Gao Cheng wished to drive a wedge between Hou Jing and Liang, and wrote to Jing with falsified wording, saying he had originally sent Jing to stir rebellion at Jingyang and meant to plot the west together; when Western Wei learned of it, Jing turned instead to plotting with the south.
units.literal: The Prince wished to drive a wedge between Jing and Liang, and wrote to Jing with falsified wording, saying he had originally had Jing stir rebellion at Jingyang and planned with him to strike west; when Western Wei learned this, Jing turned instead to scheming with the south.

units.zh: 壬申，東魏主與王獵於鄴東，馳逐如飛。
units.en: On renshen the Eastern Wei emperor hunted with Gao Cheng east of Ye, galloping as if in flight.
units.literal: On renshen, the Eastern Wei emperor hunted with the Prince east of Ye, racing as if flying.

units.zh: 監衛都督烏那羅受工伐從後呼曰：「天子莫走馬，大將軍怒。」
units.en: Supervisory Guard Commander Wunaluo Shougongfa shouted from behind, "Your Majesty, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!"
units.literal: Supervisory Guard Commander Wunaluo Shougongfa shouted from behind: "Your Majesty, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!"

units.zh: 王怒曰：「朕！
units.en: Gao Cheng raged, "Imperial We!
units.literal: The Prince raged: "Imperial We!

units.zh: 東魏主賜季舒彩，季舒未敢即受，啟之於王，王使取一段。
units.en: The Eastern Wei emperor bestowed silk on Jishu; Jishu dared not accept at once and reported to Gao Cheng, who told him to take one bolt.
units.literal: The Eastern Wei emperor bestowed silk on Jishu; Jishu dared not accept at once and reported to the Prince, who told him to take one bolt.

units.zh: 三月辛亥，王南臨黎陽，濟於虎牢，自洛陽從太行而反晉陽。
units.en: On xinhai of the third month Gao Cheng went south to Liyang, crossed at Hulao, and returned to Jinyang from Luoyang by way of the Taihang.
units.literal: On xinhai of the third month, the Prince went south to Liyang, crossed at Hulao, and returned to Jinyang by way of Taihang from Luoyang.

units.zh: 六月，王巡北邊城戍，賑賜有差。
units.en: In the sixth month Gao Cheng toured the northern border forts and gave relief in varying measure.
units.literal: In the sixth month the Prince toured northern border forts and gave relief in varying measure.

units.zh: 七月，王還晉陽。
units.en: In the seventh month Gao Cheng returned to Jinyang.
units.literal: In the seventh month the Prince returned to Jinyang.

units.zh: 識者以為王將殂之兆也。
units.en: Those who understood took it as an omen that Gao Cheng would die.
units.literal: Those who understood took it as an omen that the Prince would die.

units.zh: 初，梁將蘭欽子京為東魏所虜，王命以配廚。
units.en: Earlier, Zi Jing, son of the Liang general Lan Qin, had been captured by Eastern Wei; Gao Cheng ordered him assigned to the kitchen staff.
units.literal: Earlier, Zi Jing, son of Liang General Lan Qin, had been captured by Eastern Wei; the Prince ordered him assigned to the kitchen staff.

units.zh: 欽請贖之，王不許。
units.en: Lan Qin asked to ransom him; Gao Cheng refused.
units.literal: Lan Qin asked to ransom him; the Prince refused.

units.zh: 京再訴，王使監廚蒼頭薛豐洛杖之，曰：「更訴當殺爾。」
units.en: Jing appealed again; Gao Cheng had the kitchen-overseer bondman Xue Fengluo beat him and said, "Complain again and you will be killed."
units.literal: Jing appealed again; the Prince had kitchen-overseer bondman Xue Fengluo beat him and said: "Complain again and you will be killed."

units.zh: 王曰：「小人新杖之，故嚇我耳。」
units.en: Gao Cheng said, "That wretch was just flogged—he only wants to frighten me."
units.literal: The Prince said: "That wretch was just flogged—he only wants to frighten me."

units.zh: 京將進食，王却，謂諸人曰：「昨夜夢此奴斫我，宜殺却。」
units.en: When Jing was about to bring food, Gao Cheng held back and told the others, "Last night I dreamed this slave hacked at me—I ought to kill him."
units.literal: When Jing was about to bring food, the Prince held back and told the others: "Last night I dreamed this slave hacked at me—I ought to kill him."

units.zh: 王怒曰：「我未索食，爾何據來！」
units.en: Gao Cheng raged, "I did not ask for food—why do you press in!"
units.literal: The Prince raged: "I did not ask for food—why do you press in!"

units.zh: 王自投傷足，入于床下。
units.en: Gao Cheng threw himself aside, wounded in the foot, and crawled under the bed.
units.literal: The Prince threw himself aside, wounded in the foot, and crawled under the bed.

units.zh: 然文襄之禍生所忽，蓋有由焉。
units.en: Yet Wenxiang's disaster grew out of what he neglected; it had its cause.
units.literal: Yet Wenxiang's disaster arose from what he neglected; there was surely a cause for it.

units.zh: 凝之弟潭之，亦有美譽。
units.en: Ningzhi's younger brother Tanzhi likewise enjoyed a fine reputation.
units.literal: Ningzhi's younger brother Tanzhi also had a fine reputation.

units.zh: 太宗世，曆尚書吏部郎，禦史中丞。
units.en: Under Emperor Taizong he served successively as director in the Ministry of Personnel and as Imperial Censor.
units.literal: In the era of Emperor Taizong he successively served as director in the Ministry of Personnel and as Imperial Censor.

units.zh: 後廢帝元徽中，為左民尚書，卒官。
units.en: Under the deposed emperor, during the Yuanhui era, he served as Minister of the Left for the People and died in office.
units.literal: Under the deposed emperor, in the Yuanhui era, he was Minister of the Left for the People and died in office.

units.zh: 潭之弟澄之，太子左積弩將軍。
units.en: Tanzhi's younger brother Chengzhi served as Left Master of Strong Crossbows in the heir apparent's household.
units.literal: Tanzhi's younger brother Chengzhi was Left Master of Strong Crossbows in the Heir Apparent's household.

units.zh: 與懷朔省事雲中司馬子如及秀容人劉貴、中山人賈顯智為奔走之友，懷朔戶曹史孫騰、外兵史侯景亦相友結。
units.en: He made running companions of Sima Ziru, affairs clerk at Huaishuo's Yunzhong desk, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan; Sun Teng, the garrison household clerk, and Hou Jing, clerk for external military affairs, joined their circle as well.
units.literal: With Sima Ziru, affairs clerk of Yunzhong at Huaishuo, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan he formed a band of comrades ready to run errands; Sun Teng, household clerk at Huaishuo, and Hou Jing, clerk in external military affairs, also joined in friendship.

units.zh: 祖祕道，梁安成王田曹參軍。
units.en: His grandfather Midao had been field-cadet in the Prince of Ancheng's staff under Liang.
units.literal: His grandfather Midao was Liang field-cadet in the Prince of Ancheng's establishment.

units.zh: 三月，齊遣其上黨王高渙送貞陽侯蕭淵明來主梁嗣，至東關，遣吳興太守裴之橫與戰，敗績，之橫死。
units.en: In the third month Qi sent Prince of Shangdang Gao Huan to escort Zhenyang marquis Xiao Yuanming to take the Liang succession; at Dong Pass Wuxing administrator Pei Zhiheng fought them and was defeated and killed.
units.literal: In the third month, Qi sent its Prince of Shangdang Gao Huan to escort Marquis of Zhenyang Xiao Yuanming to assume the Liang succession; reaching Dong Pass, they sent Wuxing Administrator Pei Zhiheng to fight; defeated in battle, Zhiheng died.

units.zh: 七月辛丑，王僧辯納貞陽侯蕭淵明，自採石濟江。
units.en: On xinchou in the seventh month Wang Sengbian received Zhenyang marquis Xiao Yuanming and crossed from Caishi.
units.literal: On xinchou in the seventh month Wang Sengbian received Marquis of Zhenyang Xiao Yuanming and crossed the river from Caishi.

units.zh: 九月甲辰，司空陳霸先舉義，襲殺王僧辯，黜蕭淵明。
units.en: On jiachen in the ninth month Minister of Works Chen Baxian rose in revolt, killed Wang Sengbian in a surprise attack, and deposed Xiao Yuanming.
units.literal: On jiachen in the ninth month Minister of Works Chen Baxian raised righteousness, launched a surprise attack and killed Wang Sengbian, and deposed Xiao Yuanming.

units.zh: 以貞陽侯淵明爲司徒，封建安郡公，食邑三千戶。
units.en: Zhenyang marquis Yuanming was made Minister of Education and enfeoffed as Duke of Jian'an with three thousand households.
units.literal: Marquis of Zhenyang Yuanming was made Minister of Education, enfeoffed Duke of Jian'an commandery with fief of three thousand households.

units.zh: 癸丑，進太尉蕭循爲太保，新除司徒建安公淵明爲太傅，司徒蕭勃爲太尉。
units.en: On guichou Grand Master of War Xiao Xun was promoted to Grand Mentor; newly appointed Minister of Education Duke of Jian'an Yuanming became Grand Tutor; Minister of Education Xiao Bo became Grand Master of War.
units.literal: On guichou Grand Master of War Xiao Xun was advanced to Grand Mentor, newly appointed Minister of Education Duke of Jian'an Yuanming was made Grand Tutor, and Minister of Education Xiao Bo was made Grand Master of War.

units.zh: 五月癸未，太傅建安公淵明薨。
units.en: In the fifth month, on guiwei day, Yuanming, Duke of Jian'an and grand tutor, died.
units.literal: In the fifth month, on guiwei day, Grand Tutor Duke Yuanming of Jian'an died.

units.zh: 琰子翽問之，玄明曰：「我臨去當告卿。」
units.en: Yan's son Ao asked him for advice. Xuanming said, 'When I am about to leave office I will tell you.'
units.literal: Yan's son Ao asked him. Xuanming said, 'When I am about to leave I shall tell you.'

units.zh: 傅僧祐，祖父弘仁，高祖外弟也。
units.en: Fu Shengyou's grandfather Hongren was the Founding Emperor's brother-in-law.
units.literal: Fu Shengyou — his grandfather Hongren was younger brother by marriage to the Founding Emperor.

units.zh: 以中表曆顯官，征虜將軍、南譙太守，太常卿。
units.en: Through family connections he rose through prominent posts, serving as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, governor of Nanqiao, and Minister of Ceremonies.
units.literal: Through maternal kin ties he successively held eminent offices: General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, governor of Nanqiao, and Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 子邵，員外散騎侍郎，妻燾女也，生僧祐，有吏才，再為山陰令，甚有能名，末世令長莫及。
units.en: His son Shao served as Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, married Dao's daughter, and fathered Shengyou. Shengyou had a gift for administration, served twice as magistrate of Shanyin with great renown, and in the dynasty's final years no district magistrate could rival him.
units.literal: His son Shao was Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry; he married Dao's daughter and fathered Shengyou, who had talent for administration, twice served as magistrate of Shanyin with a great reputation for competence, and at the end of the dynasty no district magistrate could match him.

units.zh: 壬辰，封當陽公大心為尋陽郡王，石城公大款為江夏郡王，寧國公大臨為南海郡王，臨城公大連為南郡王，西豊公大春為安陸郡王，新塗公大成為山陽郡王，臨湘公大封為宜都郡王。
units.en: On renchen Duke Daxin of Dangyang became Prince of Xunyang, Duke Dakuan of Shicheng Prince of Jiangxia, Duke Dalin of Ningguo Prince of Nanhai, Duke Dalian of Lincheng Prince of Nan commandery, Duke Dachun of Xifeng Prince of Anlu, Duke Dacheng of Xintu Prince of Shanyang, and Duke Dafeng of Linxiang Prince of Yidu.
units.literal: On renchen Duke of Dangyang Daxin was enfeoffed as Prince of Xunyang commandery, Duke of Shicheng Dakuan as Prince of Jiangxia, Duke of Ningguo Dalin as Prince of Nanhai, Duke of Lincheng Dalian as Prince of Nan commandery, Duke of Xifeng Dachun as Prince of Anlu, Duke of Xintu Dacheng as Prince of Shanyang, Duke of Linxiang Dafeng as Prince of Yidu.

units.zh: 父顒，齊中書侍郎，有名於時。
units.en: His father Yan had been a Secretariat Attendant under Qi and was well known in his day.
units.literal: His father Yan was a Secretariat Attendant of Qi and had a reputation in his time.

units.zh: 周捨字昇逸，汝南安城人，晉左光祿大夫顗之八世孫也。
units.en: Zhou She, whose courtesy name was Shengyi, came from Ancheng in Runan and was the eighth-generation descendant of Zhou Yi, who had served Jin as Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: Zhou She, styled Shengyi, was a native of Ancheng in Runan and an eighth-generation descendant of Zhou Yi, the Jin Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

units.zh: 捨幼聰潁，顒異之，臨卒謂曰：「汝不患不富貴，但當持之以道德。」
units.en: As a boy, She was quick and clever, and Yan saw something extraordinary in him. On his deathbed Yan told him, "You need not fear that you will lack wealth and rank, but you must hold yourself to moral principle."
units.literal: She in youth was clever and quick; Yan regarded him as exceptional. On his deathbed he told him, "You need not worry about lacking wealth and rank, but you must uphold yourself with moral virtue."

units.zh: 吏部尚書范雲與顒素善，重捨才器，言之於高祖，召拜尚書祠部郎。
units.en: Fan Yun, Minister of Personnel, had long been close to Yan and admired She's ability. He recommended him to the High Ancestor, who summoned She and appointed him Gentleman of the Sacrifices Section in the Secretariat.
units.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Fan Yun had long been on good terms with Yan and valued She's talent and capacity; he spoke of him to the High Ancestor, who summoned and appointed him Gentleman of the Department of Sacrifices in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 賾與河南元善、河東柳䛒、太原王劭、吳興姚察、琅琊諸葛潁、信都劉焯、河間劉炫相善，每因休假，清談竟日。
units.en: Ze was on good terms with Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bi of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langya, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on holidays they would converse in pure talk all day.
units.literal: Ze was on good terms with Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bi of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langya, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on holidays they would converse in pure talk all day.

units.zh: 列傳第十五 臧燾徐廣傅隆
units.en: Biography 15 — Zang Dao, Xu Guang, and Fu Long
units.literal: Biography 15: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long

units.zh: 臧燾，字德仁，東莞莒人，武敬皇后兄也。
units.en: Zang Dao, whose courtesy name was De Ren, came from Ju in Dongguan and was the elder brother of Empress Wu Jing.
units.literal: Zang Dao, styled De Ren, was a man of Ju in Dongguan and elder brother to Empress Wu Jing.

units.zh: 臧燾、徐廣、傅隆、裴松之、何承天、雷次宗，並服膺聖哲，不為雅俗推移，立名於世，宜矣。
units.en: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian, and Lei Cizong all devoted themselves to the sages, were not swayed by fashion, and won renown in their age — as was only fitting.
units.literal: Zang Dao, Xu Guang, Fu Long, Pei Songzhi, He Chengtian, and Lei Cizong all embraced the sage and wise in their hearts, were not shifted by elegant fashion or vulgar custom, and established names in the world — as was fitting.

units.zh: 少好學，善《三禮》，貧約自立，操行為鄉里所稱。
units.en: From an early age he devoted himself to study and excelled in the Three Rites. Though poor, he made his own way, and his moral bearing won praise throughout his home district.
units.literal: In youth he loved learning, was skilled in the Three Rites, supported himself in poverty and frugality, and his conduct was praised in his district.

units.zh: 晉孝武帝太元中，衛將軍謝安始立國學，徐、兗二州刺史謝玄舉燾為助教。
units.en: During the Taixuan reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Defender-General Xie An founded the National Academy for the first time, and Xie Xuan, inspector of Xu and Yan, recommended Dao to serve as an assistant instructor.
units.literal: In the Taixuan era of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Defender-General Xie An first established the National Academy, and Xie Xuan, regional inspector of Xu and Yan, recommended Dao as assistant instructor.

units.zh: 高祖受命，征拜太常，雖外戚貴顯，而彌自沖約，茅屋蔬餐，不改其舊。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, Dao was summoned as Minister of Ceremonies; though he was now a prominent imperial kinsman, he became only more restrained, keeping to his thatched dwelling and plain meals as before.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate he was summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonies; though a prominent maternal relative, he became only more self-restrained and modest, living in thatched huts on vegetable fare without changing his former ways.

units.zh: 襲封高陵亭侯。
units.en: He inherited the title Marquis of Gaoling district.
units.literal: He inherited enfeoffment as Marquis of Gaoling district.

units.zh: 以母老家貧，與弟熹俱棄人事，躬耕自業，約己養親者十餘載。
units.en: His mother was old and the family poor, so he and his younger brother Xi withdrew from public life, worked the fields with their own hands, and for more than ten years lived frugally to support their parents.
units.literal: Because his mother was aged and his family poor, he and his younger brother Xi together abandoned worldly affairs, tilled the fields themselves to make their living, and for more than ten years restrained themselves to support their kin.

units.zh: 父母喪亡，居喪六年，以毀瘠著稱。
units.en: After his parents died he mourned for six years and became famous for the wasting grief that marked his observance.
units.literal: When his parents died he observed mourning for six years and became renowned for emaciation from grief.

units.zh: 長子邃，護軍司馬，宜都太守。
units.en: His eldest son Sui served as marshal of the Protector Army and as governor of Yidu.
units.literal: His eldest son Sui was marshal of the Protector Army and governor of Yidu.

units.zh: 少子綽，太子中舍人，新安太守。
units.en: His younger son Chuo served as attendant in the heir apparent's household and as governor of Xin'an.
units.literal: His younger son Chuo was attendant in the household of the Heir Apparent and governor of Xin'an.

units.zh: 義熙十四年，除侍中。
units.en: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he was appointed Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he was appointed Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 元熙元年，以腳疾去職。
units.en: In the first year of Yuanxi he resigned because of a foot ailment.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanxi he left office because of foot ailment.

units.zh: 永初三年，致仕，拜光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。
units.en: In the third year of Yongchu he retired and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple cord.
units.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he retired from office, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and granted the golden seal and purple cord.

units.zh: 其年卒，時年七十。
units.en: He died the same year, at the age of seventy.
units.literal: That year he died, aged seventy.

units.zh: 服闋，除臨沂令。
units.en: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed magistrate of Linyi.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed magistrate of Linyi.

units.zh: 燾議曰：「《陽秋》，之義，母以子貴，故仲子、成風，咸稱夫人。
units.en: Dao argued in a memorial: "According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, a mother is elevated through her son's rank; that is why Zhong Zi and Cheng Feng were both addressed as Lady.
units.literal: Dao submitted a memorial saying: "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that a mother is ennobled through her son; therefore Zhong Zi and Cheng Feng were both styled Lady.

units.zh: 《經》云'考仲子之宮'。
units.en: The Classic states, 'Inspect the temple of Zhong Zi.'
units.literal: The Classic says, 'Inspect the temple of Zhong Zi.'

units.zh: 若配食惠廟，則宮無緣別築。
units.en: If she were given a place in Emperor Hui's temple, there would be no occasion to erect a separate shrine.
units.literal: If she were to share offerings in the temple of Emperor Hui, there would be no reason to build a separate temple.

units.zh: 前漢孝文、孝昭太后，並系子為號，祭於寢園，不配于高祖、孝武之廟。
units.en: In Former Han, the empress dowagers Wen and Zhao both bore titles tied to their sons, received sacrifice in the tomb-park shrines, and were not installed as consorts in the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu.
units.literal: The empress dowagers Wen and Zhao of Former Han both took titles derived from their sons, were sacrificed to in the park shrines at their tombs, and were not paired in the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu.

units.zh: 後漢和帝之母曰恭懷皇所，安帝祖母曰敬隱皇后，順帝之母曰恭湣皇后，雖不系子為號，亦祭於陵寢。
units.en: In Later Han, Emperor He's mother was known as Empress Gonghuai, Emperor An's grandmother as Empress Jingyin, and Emperor Shun's mother as Empress Gongmin; although their titles were not framed through their sons' reign names, they likewise received sacrifice at the tomb shrines.
units.literal: In Later Han, the mother of Emperor He was called Empress Gonghuai, the grandmother of Emperor An was called Empress Jingyin, and the mother of Emperor Shun was called Empress Gongmin; though their titles were not derived from their sons, they too were sacrificed to at the tomb shrines.

units.zh: 不配章、安二帝。
units.en: None of them was paired with the temples of Emperors Zhang and An.
units.literal: They were not paired with Emperors Zhang and An.

units.zh: 此則二漢雖有太后、皇后之異，至於並不配食，義同《陽秋》。
units.en: Thus, although Former and Later Han differed in whether the women were styled empress dowager or empress, in neither dynasty were they given shared temple offerings — a principle in keeping with the Spring and Autumn Annals.
units.literal: Thus although the two Han differed as to empress dowager and empress, in neither case were they given shared offerings, in the same sense as the Spring and Autumn Annals.

units.zh: 唯光武追廢呂後，故以薄後配高祖廟。
units.en: Only under Guangwu, who posthumously deposed Empress Lü, was Empress Bo installed as consort in Gaozu's temple.
units.literal: Only Guangwu, in posthumously deposing Empress Lü, therefore paired Empress Bo in the temple of Gaozu.

units.zh: 又衛後既廢，霍光追尊李夫人為皇后，配孝武廟，此非母以子貴之例，直以高、武二廟無配故耳。
units.en: Again, after Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously honored Lady Li as empress and paired her with Emperor Wu's temple; that was not an instance of a mother elevated through her son, but merely because the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu had lacked consorts.
units.literal: Again, after Empress Wei was deposed, Huo Guang posthumously honored Lady Li as empress and paired her in the temple of Emperor Wu; this was not a case of a mother ennobled through her son, but simply because the temples of Gaozu and Emperor Wu lacked consorts.

units.zh: 夫漢立寢於陵，自是晉制所異。
units.en: Han practice of erecting tomb shrines at the mausoleums was in any case unlike Jin custom.
units.literal: That Han established tomb shrines at the mausoleums was itself something Jin institutions differed from.

units.zh: 謂宜遠准《陽秋》考宮之義，近摹二漢不配之典。
units.en: I submit that we should take as our distant standard the Annals' principle of the separate temple, and as our near precedent the two Han rule against shared offerings.
units.literal: I hold that one should take as distant standard the Annals' meaning of inspecting the temple, and as near model the two Han precedent of not pairing offerings.

units.zh: 尊號既正，則罔極之情申，別建寢廟，則嚴禰之義顯，系子為稱，兼明母貴之所由，一舉而允三義，固哲王之高致也。」
