units.en: Once her title is properly fixed, the fullest measure of filial devotion is expressed; if a separate shrine is built, the solemn dignity of ancestral worship is preserved; and framing her title through her son's name makes clear the source of her elevation — to satisfy all three principles in a single measure is truly the mark of a sage ruler."
units.literal: Once the honorific title is correct, boundless filial feeling is expressed; if a separate tomb shrine is built, the solemn meaning of ancestral sacrifice is displayed; taking the son's name in the title also clarifies whence the mother's nobility derives — one act satisfying three principles is indeed the lofty aim of a sage king."

units.zh: 乃上議曰：「臣聞國之大事，在祀與戎，將營宮室，宗廟為首。
units.en: He then submitted a memorial: "I have heard that the great affairs of a state are sacrifice and war, and that when palaces are to be built, the ancestral temple must come first.
units.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that the great affairs of a state are sacrifice and war; when palace buildings are to be planned, the ancestral temple comes first.

units.zh: 古先哲王，莫不致肅恭之誠心，盡崇嚴乎祖考，然後能流淳化于四海，通幽感於神明。
units.en: The sage kings of antiquity all brought reverent sincerity to their rites and showed the utmost honor to their ancestors; only then could pure teaching spread through the realm and the unseen world respond to their devotion.
units.literal: The sage kings of antiquity all devoted reverent and sincere hearts and showed the utmost honor to their forefathers, and only then could pure transformation flow through the four seas and hidden feeling reach the spirits.

units.zh: 固宜詳廢興於古典，循情禮以求中者也。
units.en: One ought therefore to weigh abolition and establishment against the ancient canon and seek the mean in light of ritual and human feeling.
units.literal: One should indeed examine abolition and establishment in the ancient canon and follow sentiment and ritual to seek the mean.

units.zh: 禮，天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖而七。
units.en: According to ritual, the Son of Heaven keeps seven temples — three zhao and three mu, with the Great Ancestor, for a total of seven.
units.literal: Ritual prescribes seven temples for the Son of Heaven: three zhao and three mu, with the Great Ancestor making seven.

units.zh: 自考廟以至祖考五廟，皆月祭之，遠廟為祧，有二祧，享嘗乃止。
units.en: From the temple of the immediate forebear down through the five temples of more distant ancestors, all receive monthly sacrifice; the most remote temples become tiao, and once there are two tiao, only the seasonal offerings remain.
units.literal: From the temple of the father down to the five temples of the ancestors, all receive monthly sacrifice; distant temples become tiao, and when there are two tiao, only the seasonal offerings continue.

units.zh: 去祧為壇，去壇為墠，有禱然後祭之。
units.en: When the tiao are removed they become altars; when the altars are removed they become open ritual mounds; and sacrifice is offered only when prayer is required.
units.literal: When the tiao are removed they become altars; when the altars are removed they become open mounds; sacrifice is made only when there is prayer.

units.zh: 此宗廟之次，親疏之序也。
units.en: Such is the order of the ancestral temples and the gradation of kinship from near to remote.
units.literal: This is the order of the ancestral temples and the sequence of near and remote kinship.

units.zh: 鄭玄以為祧者文王、武王之廟，王肅以為五世六世之祖。
units.en: Zheng Xuan held that the tiao were the temples of Kings Wen and Wu, whereas Wang Su held that they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.
units.literal: Zheng Xuan held that the tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held that they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.

units.zh: 尋去祧之言，則祧非文、武之廟矣。
units.en: If we examine the phrase 'removing the tiao,' the tiao cannot be the temples of Wen and Wu.
units.literal: Examining the phrase 'removing the tiao,' the tiao cannot be the temples of Wen and Wu.

units.zh: 文、武周之祖宗，何雲去祧為壇乎？
units.en: Wen and Wu were Zhou's founding ancestors — how could the rites speak of removing the tiao to make altars?
units.literal: Wen and Wu were the founding ancestors of Zhou — how could one speak of removing the tiao to make altars?

units.zh: 明遠廟為祧者，無服之祖也。
units.en: This makes clear that temples made tiao are ancestors beyond the range of mourning obligation.
units.literal: This shows that distant temples made tiao are ancestors beyond the scope of mourning garments.

units.zh: 又遠廟則有享嘗之禮，去祧則有壇墠之殊，明世遠者，其義彌疏也。
units.en: Moreover, distant temples still receive seasonal offerings, whereas removed tiao are reduced to altars and open mounds — showing that the farther the generation, the more attenuated the ritual becomes.
units.literal: Again, distant temples still have the seasonal offering rites, while removed tiao have the distinction of altars and mounds — showing that the more remote the generation, the more attenuated the rite.

units.zh: 若祧是文、武之廟，宜同月祭于太祖，雖推後稷以配天，由功德之所始，非尊崇之義每有差降也。
units.en: If the tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu, they ought to receive monthly sacrifice together with the Great Ancestor; although Hou Ji was elevated to match Heaven, that was because merit began with him, not because the principle of honor allows no gradation.
units.literal: If the tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu, they ought likewise to receive monthly sacrifice with the Great Ancestor; although Hou Ji was elevated to match Heaven, that was because merit and virtue began with him, not because the meaning of honor admits no gradation.

units.zh: 又禮有以多貴者，故傳稱德厚者流光，德薄者流卑。
units.en: Ritual also holds that greater merit confers greater honor; hence the tradition says that abundant virtue casts its radiance far, while meager virtue casts it low.
units.literal: Again, ritual has the principle that abundance confers honor; therefore the tradition says that thick virtue casts its light far, while thin virtue casts it low.

units.zh: 又雲自上以下，降殺以兩，禮也。
units.en: It also says that from higher to lower ranks, ritual diminishes by steps of two.
units.literal: It also says that from above to below, diminution proceeds by twos — such is ritual.

units.zh: 此則尊卑等級之典，上下殊異之文。
units.en: This is the canon governing rank and precedence, the written rule distinguishing higher from lower.
units.literal: This is the canon of noble and base ranks and the text of distinction between higher and lower.

units.zh: 而雲天子諸侯俱祭五廟，何哉？
units.en: Yet how can it be said that the Son of Heaven and the feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples?
units.literal: Yet it says that Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples — how so?

units.zh: 又王祭嫡殤，下及來孫，而上祀之禮，不過高祖。
units.en: Again, the king may sacrifice for legitimate heirs who died young, extending down to remote descendants, yet the rite of ascending sacrifice goes no higher than the great-grandfather.
units.literal: Again, the king sacrifices for legitimate heirs who died young, extending down to remote descendants, yet the rite of ascending sacrifice goes no higher than the great-grandfather.

units.zh: 推隆恩於下流，替誠敬於尊屬，亦非聖人制禮之意也。
units.en: To extend lavish favor downward while displacing sincere reverence owed to honored forebears is not what the sages intended when they established ritual.
units.literal: To extend exalted favor downstream while displacing sincere reverence for honored kin is also not the intent of the sages in establishing ritual.

units.zh: 是以泰始建廟，從王氏議，以禮父為士，子為天子諸侯，祭以天子諸侯，其屍服以士服。
units.en: Therefore, when the Taishi temples were established, Wang's proposal was adopted: by ritual the father had been a common officer while the son became Son of Heaven or feudal lord; sacrifice was performed with royal rites, but the impersonator wore an officer's garment.
units.literal: Therefore when the Taishi temples were established, Wang's proposal was followed: by ritual the father was a common officer and the son became Son of Heaven or feudal lord; sacrifice was offered as to Son of Heaven or feudal lord, but the impersonator's garment was the officer's robe.

units.zh: 故上及征西，以備六世之數，宣皇雖為太祖，尚在子孫之位，至於殷祭之日，未申東向之禮，所謂子雖齊聖，不先父食者矣。
units.en: Sacrifice therefore extended up to the Western Campaign lord to complete six generations; although Emperor Xuan was the Great Ancestor, he still occupied the position of a descendant, and on the day of the great seasonal sacrifice the rite of facing east had not yet been accorded him — illustrating the rule that even a sage son does not take precedence over his father at the offering.
units.literal: Thus sacrifice extended up to the Western Campaign lord to complete the count of six generations; although Emperor Xuan was the Great Ancestor, he still stood in the place of a descendant, and on the day of the great seasonal sacrifice the rite of facing east had not yet been performed for him — what is called 'though the son be equal to a sage, he does not take precedence over his father in eating.'

units.zh: 今京兆以上既遷，太祖始得居正，議者以昭穆未足，欲屈太祖于卑坐，臣以為非禮典之旨。
units.en: Now that the shrines above Jingzhao have been moved, the Great Ancestor can at last take the central position; some debaters, believing the zhao and mu are not yet complete, wish to place the Great Ancestor in a lower seat — I hold that this violates the intent of the ritual canon.
units.literal: Now that those above Jingzhao have been moved, the Great Ancestor can at last take the central place; debaters, holding that the zhao and mu are not yet complete, wish to place the Great Ancestor in a lower seat — I hold that this is not the intent of the ritual canon.

units.zh: 所與太祖而七，自是昭穆既足，太祖在六世之外，非為須滿七廟，乃得居太祖也。
units.en: 'Seven temples with the Great Ancestor' means that the zhao and mu are already complete; the Great Ancestor stands beyond the sixth generation — he does not need seven temples to be filled before he may take the position of Great Ancestor.
units.literal: 'With the Great Ancestor, seven' means that the zhao and mu are already complete; the Great Ancestor stands beyond the sixth generation — it is not that one must fill seven temples before he may occupy the place of Great Ancestor.

units.zh: 議者又以四府君神主宜永同于殷祫，臣又以為不然。
units.en: The debaters also argued that the spirit tablets of the four lords ought forever to share the great seasonal sacrifice — I again held that this was wrong.
units.literal: The debaters also held that the spirit tablets of the four lords ought forever to share the great seasonal sacrifice — I again held that this was wrong.

units.zh: 傳所謂毀廟之主，陳乎太祖，謂太祖以下先君之主也。
units.en: What the tradition calls 'the tablets of abolished temples displayed before the Great Ancestor' refers to the tablets of former lords below the Great Ancestor.
units.literal: What the tradition calls 'the tablets of abolished temples displayed before the Great Ancestor' means the tablets of former lords below the Great Ancestor.

units.zh: 故《白虎通》雲「禘祫祭遷廟者，以其繼君之體，持其統而不絕也。」
units.en: Thus the Comprehensive Meaning states: 'The great seasonal sacrifices for moved temples are offered because those ancestors embodied succession to the lordship and preserved the line without break.'
units.literal: Therefore the Comprehensive Meaning says: 'The great seasonal sacrifices for moved temples are because they embody succession to the lordship and maintain the line without break.'

units.zh: 豈如四府君在太祖之前乎。
units.en: How could the four lords stand before the Great Ancestor?
units.literal: How could the four lords stand before the Great Ancestor?

units.zh: 非繼統之主，無靈命之瑞，非王業之基，昔以世近而及，今則情禮已遠，而當長饗殷祫，永虛太祖之位，求之禮籍，未見其可。
units.en: They were not rulers who succeeded to the throne, bore no mandate confirmed by heavenly signs, and were not the foundation of the royal enterprise; they were included before only because the generations were near, but now feeling and ritual have grown remote, yet they are to receive the great seasonal sacrifice forever while the Great Ancestor's place remains empty — I find no approval for this in the ritual canon.
units.literal: They were not lords who succeeded to the line, bore no auspicious mandate of the spirits, and were not the foundation of royal enterprise; formerly they were included because the generation was near, but now sentiment and ritual are remote, yet they are to receive the great seasonal sacrifice forever and leave the Great Ancestor's place eternally vacant — sought in the ritual records, I do not see how this can be approved.

units.zh: 昔永和之初，大議斯禮，于時虞喜、范宣並以淵儒碩學，鹹謂四府君神主，無緣永存於百世。
units.en: At the beginning of the Yonghe era this ritual was debated at length; Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both profound and accomplished scholars, agreed that the spirit tablets of the four lords had no grounds to endure for a hundred generations.
units.literal: In the beginning of the Yonghe era this ritual was debated at length; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both profound scholars of vast learning, all held that the spirit tablets of the four lords had no reason to endure for a hundred generations.

units.zh: 或欲瘞之兩階，或欲藏之石室，或欲為之改築，雖所秉小異，而大歸是同。
units.en: Some proposed burying the tablets between the temple steps, others storing them in the stone chamber, others rebuilding shrines for them; though their particular proposals differed, they agreed in principle.
units.literal: Some wished to bury them between the steps, some to store them in the stone chamber, some to rebuild shrines for them; though their particular views differed slightly, the main conclusion was the same.

units.zh: 若宣皇既居群廟之上，而四主禘祫不已，則大晉殷祭，長無太祖之位矣。
units.en: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the other temples while the four lords continue forever in the great seasonal sacrifice, then in Jin's great seasonal rites the Great Ancestor's place will remain permanently empty.
units.literal: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the mass of temples while the four lords continue in the great seasonal sacrifice without end, then in the great Jin seasonal rites the place of the Great Ancestor will forever be vacant.

units.zh: 夫理貴有中，不必過厚；
units.en: Ritual principle values the mean and need not be excessive;
units.literal: Principle values hitting the mean and need not be excessive;

units.zh: 禮與世遷，豈可順而不斷！
units.en: ritual changes with the times — how can one follow custom without ever drawing a line!
units.literal: ritual shifts with the age — how can one follow it without making a break!

units.zh: 故臣子之情雖篤，而靈厲之諡彌彰；
units.en: Thus although a subject's devotion may run deep, the posthumous title of the departed grows ever more distinct;
units.literal: Thus although the feeling of subject and son is deep, the posthumous title of the departed spirit grows ever more distinct;

units.zh: 追遠之懷雖切，而遷毀之禮為用。
units.en: and although longing for the distant past may be intense, the rite of moving and abolishing temples is what must govern.
units.literal: although longing to reach the remote past is keen, the rite of moving and abolishing temples is what applies.

units.zh: 豈不有心于加厚，顧禮制不可逾爾。
units.en: It is not that the heart lacks desire to show greater honor, but ritual cannot be overstepped.
units.literal: Is it not that one has a mind to add still more honor, yet ritual institutions cannot be transgressed?

units.zh: 石室則藏於廟北，改築則未知所處，虞主所以依神，神移則有 瘞埋之禮。
units.en: The stone chamber lies north of the temple; rebuilding would leave their resting place uncertain; the provisional tablet lodges the spirit, and when the spirit is transferred there is a rite of burial.
units.literal: The stone chamber lies north of the temple; rebuilding would leave the place unknown; the provisional tablet exists to lodge the spirit — when the spirit moves, there is the rite of burial.

units.zh: 四主若饗祀宜廢，亦神之所不依也，准傍事例，宜同虞主之瘞埋。
units.en: If sacrifice to the four lords ought to cease, their spirits likewise have no further lodging; following parallel precedents, their tablets should be buried as provisional tablets are.
units.literal: If sacrifice to the four lords ought to be abolished, the spirits likewise have no lodging; following parallel precedents, they should be buried like provisional tablets.

units.zh: 然經典難詳，群言紛錯，非臣卑淺所能折中。」
units.en: Yet the classics are difficult to pin down and opinions conflict; this is more than my limited learning can reconcile."
units.literal: Yet the classics are hard to detail fully and many opinions tangle and clash — this is not something my lowly shallowness can reconcile."

units.zh: 議者從之。
units.en: The assembly adopted his view.
units.literal: The debaters followed him.

units.zh: 時學者多從燾議，竟未施行。
units.en: At the time most scholars sided with Dao, but in the end his proposal was not implemented.
units.literal: At the time most scholars followed Dao's proposal, but in the end it was not carried out.

units.zh: 少帝追贈左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。
units.en: Emperor Shao posthumously honored him as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
units.literal: Emperor Shao posthumously awarded him Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and added the title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

units.zh: 高祖鎮京口，與燾書曰：「頃學尚廢弛，後進頹業，衡門之內，清風輟響。
units.en: While stationed at Jingkou, the Founding Emperor wrote to Dao: "Learning has lately fallen into neglect, the younger generation's devotion to study has waned, and within humble households the voice of upright conduct has fallen silent.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor was stationed at Jingkou he wrote to Dao: "Recently learning has been neglected and slack, the younger generation's pursuit of study has declined, and within humble doorways the sound of pure conduct has ceased.

units.zh: 時太廟鴟尾災，燾謂著作郎徐廣曰：「昔孔子在齊，聞魯廟災，曰必桓、僖也。
units.en: When fire broke out at the finials of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Dao said to Xu Guang of the Master of Writings office: "Long ago, when Confucius was in Qi and heard that Lu's ancestral temple had burned, he said the disaster must concern the shrines of Duke Huan and Duke Xi.
units.literal: At that time the temple finials of the Imperial Ancestral Temple caught fire; Dao said to Xu Guang, Master of Writings: "Formerly when Confucius was in Qi and heard of fire in the Lu temple, he said it must concern Huan and Xi.

units.zh: 高祖北伐關、洛，大司馬琅邪王同行，除大司馬從事中郎，總留府事。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor marched north against Guanzhong and Luoyang, the Prince of Langye, serving as Grand Marshal, accompanied the campaign; Dao was appointed attendant gentleman on the Grand Marshal's staff and took charge of all affairs left behind at headquarters.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor marched north against Guan and Luo, the Prince of Langye, Grand Marshal, accompanied him; Dao was appointed attendant gentleman of the Grand Marshal and oversaw all affairs left at headquarters.

units.zh: 傅琰 虞愿 劉懷慰 裴昭明 沈憲 李珪之 孔琇之
units.en: Fu Yan, Yu Yuan, Liu Huaiwei, Pei Zhaoming, Shen Xian, Li Guizhi, and Kong Xiuzhi
units.literal: Fu Yan, Yu Yuan, Liu Huaiwei, Pei Zhaoming, Shen Xian, Li Guizhi, Kong Xiuzhi

units.zh: 傅琰字季珪，北地靈州人也。
units.en: Fu Yan, courtesy name Jigui, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi commandery.
units.literal: Fu Yan, style name Jigui, was a man of Lingzhou in Beidi.

units.zh: 祖邵，員外郎。
units.en: His grandfather Shao served as an outside-office gentleman.
units.literal: His grandfather Shao was a Staff Gentleman Outside the Office.

units.zh: 父僧祐，安東錄事參軍。
units.en: His father Sengyou served as recorder-adjutant under the Andong commandery.
units.literal: His father Sengyou was Recorder-Adjutant of Andong.

units.zh: 遭母喪，居南岸，隣家失火，延燒琰屋，琰抱柩不動，隣人競來赴救，乃得俱全。
units.en: During his mother's mourning he lived on the south bank. A neighbor's house caught fire and the blaze spread to Yan's dwelling. He clung to the coffin and would not move; neighbors rushed to help, and mother and coffin were saved unharmed.
units.literal: When his mother died he was in mourning, dwelling on the south bank. A neighbor's house caught fire and the blaze spread to burn Yan's house. Yan embraced the coffin and did not move; neighbors rushed in competition to rescue, and thus all was preserved intact.

units.zh: 琰美姿儀，解褐寧蠻參軍，本州主簿，寧蠻功曹。
units.en: Yan was handsome in bearing. Upon entering service he was appointed adjutant of the Pacify-the-Barbarians army, chief clerk of his native province, and records officer of that army.
units.literal: Yan was handsome in bearing. Upon entering service he was appointed adjutant of the Pacify-the-Barbarians army, chief clerk of his native province, and records officer of the Pacify-the-Barbarians army.

units.zh: 宋永光元年，補諸暨武康令，廣威將軍，除尚書左民郎，又爲武康令，將軍如故。
units.en: In the first year of Yongguang of Song he was appointed magistrate of Wukang in Zhuji, made general of expansive might, appointed gentleman of the left people section in the Masters of Writing, again made magistrate of Wukang, and retained his general's rank.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongguang of Song he was appointed magistrate of Wukang in Zhuji, made General of Expansive Might, appointed gentleman of the left people section in the Masters of Writing, again made magistrate of Wukang, with his general's rank unchanged.

units.zh: 除吳興郡丞。
units.en: He was appointed assistant administrator of Wuxing commandery.
units.literal: He was appointed assistant administrator of Wuxing commandery.

units.zh: 泰始六年，遷山陰令。
units.en: In the sixth year of Taishi he was appointed magistrate of Shanyin.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi he was transferred to magistrate of Shanyin.

units.zh: 山陰，東土大縣，難爲長官，僧祐在縣有稱，琰尤明察，又著能名。
units.en: Shanyin was a major district in the eastern region and a difficult post for any magistrate. Sengyou had earned a reputation there, and Yan was especially sharp-eyed in judgment, winning renown for his competence as well.
units.literal: Shanyin was a great district of the eastern lands, difficult to govern as chief official. Sengyou had a reputation in the district; Yan was especially perspicacious and also gained a name for ability.

units.zh: 其年爵新亭侯。
units.en: That same year he was ennobled as Marquis of Xinting.
units.literal: That year he was ennobled as Marquis of Xinting.

units.zh: 元徽初，遷尚書右丞。
units.en: At the beginning of the Yuanhui reign he was promoted to right assistant director in the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui he was transferred to Right Assistant of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 琰股髀之閒，已被煙焰。
units.en: The flesh between his thighs had already been scorched by smoke and flame.
units.literal: Between Yan's thighs and buttocks he had already been touched by smoke and flame.

units.zh: 服闋，除邵陵王左軍諮議，江夏王錄事參軍。
units.en: When mourning ended he was appointed consultant to the left army of the Prince of Shaoling and recorder-adjutant to the Prince of Jiangxia.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Consultant of the Left Army under the Prince of Shaoling and Recorder-Adjutant under the Prince of Jiangxia.

units.zh: 太祖輔政，以山陰獄訟煩積，復以琰爲山陰令。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor served as regent, lawsuits in Shanyin had again piled up, so he reappointed Yan as magistrate of Shanyin.
units.literal: When the Founder assisted in government, because prison lawsuits in Shanyin piled up in annoyance, he again appointed Yan magistrate of Shanyin.

units.zh: 賣針賣糖老姥爭團絲，來詣琰，琰不辨覈，縳團絲於柱鞭之，密視有鐵屑，乃罰賣糖者。
units.en: An old woman who sold needles and one who sold sugar disputed a ball of silk and brought the case to Yan. Without questioning either party, he tied the silk to a pillar and whipped it; watching closely, he saw iron filings and then punished the sugar-seller.
units.literal: An old woman who sold needles and an old woman who sold sugar disputed a ball of silk thread and came before Yan. Yan did not distinguish and verify; he bound the silk ball to a pillar and flogged it, secretly watched and saw iron filings, and then punished the sugar-seller.

units.zh: 二野父爭雞，琰各問「何以食雞」，一人云「粟」，一人云「豆」，乃破雞得粟，罪言豆者。
units.en: Two peasants disputed ownership of a chicken. Yan asked each, "With what do you feed the chicken?" One said, "Millet"; the other said, "Beans." He slaughtered the bird, found millet in its crop, and punished the man who had claimed beans.
units.literal: Two countrymen disputed a chicken. Yan asked each, 'With what do you feed the chicken?' One said 'millet,' one said 'beans.' He then broke open the chicken and found millet, and punished the one who had said beans.

units.zh: 縣內稱神明，無敢復爲偷盜。
units.en: The district hailed him as uncannily wise, and no one dared steal again.
units.literal: Within the district he was called divine and perspicacious; none dared again to be thieves.

units.zh: 琰父子竝著奇績，江左鮮有。
units.en: Father and son Yan together achieved extraordinary records, rarely matched in the lands south of the Yangtze.
units.literal: Father and son Yan together achieved extraordinary records; east of the Yangtze there were few such cases.

units.zh: 世云「諸傅有《治縣譜》，子孫相傳，不以示人」。
units.en: People said, "The various Fu have a Register of Governing Districts, handed down among descendants and not shown to others."
units.literal: The age says, 'The various Fu have a Register of Governing Districts, handed down among descendants and not shown to others.'

units.zh: 昇明二年，太祖擢爲假節、督益寧二州軍事、建威將軍、益州刺史、宋寧太守。
units.en: In the second year of Shengming the Founding Emperor promoted him to provisional bearer of the staff, commander of Yi and Ning, general who establishes might, governor of Yi, and grand administrator of Songning.
units.literal: In the second year of Shengming the Founding Emperor promoted him to bearer of the provisional staff, commander of military affairs in Yi and Ning, General Who Establishes Might, governor of Yi, and grand administrator of Songning.

units.zh: 建元元年，進號寧朔將軍。
units.en: In the first year of Jianyuan his title was advanced to general who pacifies the north.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.

units.zh: 四年，徵驍騎將軍，黃門郎。
units.en: In the fourth year he was recalled as general of valiant cavalry and gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as General of Valiant Cavalry and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

units.zh: 永明二年，遷建威將軍、安陸王北中郎長史，改寧朔將軍。
units.en: In the second year of Yongming he was transferred to general who establishes might and chief clerk to the northern gentlemen of the interior under the Prince of Anlu, with his title changed to general who pacifies the north.
units.literal: In the second year of Yongming he was transferred to General Who Establishes Might and chief clerk to the Northern Gentlemen of the Interior under the Prince of Anlu; his title was changed to General Who Pacifies the North.

units.zh: 明年，徙廬陵王安西長史、南郡內史，行荊州事。
units.en: The next year he was moved to chief clerk to the pacify-the-west army under the Prince of Luling and interior minister of Nan commandery, acting governor of Jingzhou.
units.literal: The next year he was moved to chief clerk to the Pacify-the-West army under the Prince of Luling and interior minister of Nan commandery, acting in Jingzhou affairs.

units.zh: 五年，卒。
units.en: In the fifth year he died.
units.literal: In the fifth year he died.

units.zh: 琰喪西還，有詔出臨。
units.en: As Yan's coffin was borne westward, an edict ordered the emperor to attend in person.
units.literal: As Yan's coffin returned westward, an edict ordered the sovereign to come out and attend.

units.zh: 爲政未朞，擢山陰令傅琰爲益州刺史。
units.en: Early in his reign he promoted Fu Yan, the magistrate of Shanyin, to regional inspector of Yizhou.
units.literal: His governance had not yet reached its term when he promoted Fu Yan, magistrate of Shanyin, to Inspector of Yizhou.
